```
using System.Diagnostics;
using System.Reflection;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Diagnostics.HealthChecks;
using TradeBlotter.Api.Contracts;

namespace TradeBlotter.Api.Controllers;

/// <summary>
/// Heartbeat / status endpoint. Aggregates every registered health check
/// (see <c>AddHealthChecks()</c> in Program.cs) so new dependencies such as a
/// database or market-data feed only need to register a check to show up here.
/// </summary>
[ApiController]
[Route("api/health")]
public sealed class HealthController(
    HealthCheckService healthCheckService,
    IWebHostEnvironment environment,
    TimeProvider timeProvider) : ControllerBase
{
    private static readonly DateTimeOffset StartedAtUtc =
        Process.GetCurrentProcess().StartTime.ToUniversalTime();

    private static readonly string Version =
        typeof(Program).Assembly
            .GetCustomAttribute<AssemblyInformationalVersionAttribute>()?
            .InformationalVersion ?? "unknown";

    [HttpGet]
    [ProducesResponseType<HealthResponse>(StatusCodes.Status200OK)]
    [ProducesResponseType<HealthResponse>(StatusCodes.Status503ServiceUnavailable)]
    public async Task<ActionResult<HealthResponse>> Get(CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        var report = await healthCheckService.CheckHealthAsync(cancellationToken);
        var now = timeProvider.GetUtcNow();

        var response = new HealthResponse(
            Status: report.Status.ToString(),
            Service: environment.ApplicationName,
            Version: Version,
            Environment: environment.EnvironmentName,
            ServerTimeUtc: now,
            StartedAtUtc: StartedAtUtc,
            UptimeSeconds: Math.Round((now - StartedAtUtc).TotalSeconds, 1),
            TotalDurationMs: report.TotalDuration.TotalMilliseconds,
            Checks: report.Entries
                .Select(e => new HealthCheckEntry(
                    e.Key,
                    e.Value.Status.ToString(),
                    e.Value.Description,
                    e.Value.Duration.TotalMilliseconds))
                .ToList());

        // Degraded still serves traffic; only Unhealthy is reported as 503.
        var statusCode = report.Status == HealthStatus.Unhealthy
            ? StatusCodes.Status503ServiceUnavailable
            : StatusCodes.Status200OK;

        return StatusCode(statusCode, response);
    }
}

```

```
using Microsoft.Extensions.Diagnostics.HealthChecks;

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

// Add services to the container.

builder.Services.AddControllers();
// Learn more about configuring Swagger/OpenAPI at https://aka.ms/aspnetcore/swashbuckle
builder.Services.AddEndpointsApiExplorer();
builder.Services.AddSwaggerGen();

builder.Services.AddSingleton(TimeProvider.System);

// Register dependency checks here (database, market data, etc.); they are
// aggregated by GET /api/health.
builder.Services.AddHealthChecks()
    .AddCheck("self", () => HealthCheckResult.Healthy("API process is running"));

var app = builder.Build();

// Configure the HTTP request pipeline.
if (app.Environment.IsDevelopment())
{
    app.UseSwagger();
    app.UseSwaggerUI();
}

app.UseHttpsRedirection();

app.UseAuthorization();

app.MapControllers();

app.Run();
```

```
<#
.SYNOPSIS
    Runs the Trade Blotter API (.NET 8) in development mode.

.DESCRIPTION
    Starts the API on http://localhost:5035 (the "http" launch profile) with
    hot reload via `dotnet watch`. Swagger UI is at http://localhost:5035/swagger
    and the heartbeat at http://localhost:5035/api/health.

.PARAMETER NoWatch
    Run without hot reload (plain `dotnet run`).

.EXAMPLE
    .\run_api.ps1
.EXAMPLE
    .\run_api.ps1 -NoWatch
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [switch]$NoWatch
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

if (-not (Get-Command dotnet -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
    throw 'The .NET SDK was not found on PATH. Install the .NET 8 SDK: https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0'
}

$apiDir  = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'api'
$project = 'src/TradeBlotter.Api/TradeBlotter.Api.csproj'

# Run from api/ so api/global.json pins the .NET 8 SDK.
Push-Location $apiDir
try {
    $env:ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT = 'Development'
    if ($NoWatch) {
        dotnet run --project $project --launch-profile http
    }
    else {
        dotnet watch run --project $project --launch-profile http
    }
    exit $LASTEXITCODE
}
finally {
    Pop-Location
}

```

</details>

```
<#
.SYNOPSIS
    Runs the Trade Blotter frontend (Vue 3 + Vite) in development mode.

.DESCRIPTION
    Starts the Vite dev server on http://localhost:5173. Requests to /api are
    proxied to the API (see app/vite.config.ts), so start it with .\run_api.ps1.
    Dependencies are installed automatically on first run.

.PARAMETER Install
    Force `npm install` before starting (e.g. after pulling dependency changes).

.EXAMPLE
    .\run_app.ps1
.EXAMPLE
    .\run_app.ps1 -Install
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [switch]$Install
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

if (-not (Get-Command npm -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
    throw 'npm was not found on PATH. Install Node.js 22.18+ or 24.12+: https://nodejs.org/'
}

$appDir = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'app'

Push-Location $appDir
try {
    if ($Install -or -not (Test-Path 'node_modules')) {
        Write-Host 'Installing frontend dependencies...' -ForegroundColor Cyan
        npm install
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
    }

    npm run dev
    exit $LASTEXITCODE
}
finally {
    Pop-Location
}

```

```
import { fileURLToPath, URL } from 'node:url'

import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import vue from '@vitejs/plugin-vue'
import vueDevTools from 'vite-plugin-vue-devtools'

// Matches the "http" profile in api/src/TradeBlotter.Api/Properties/launchSettings.json.
const API_URL = process.env.API_URL ?? 'http://localhost:5035'

// https://vite.dev/config/
export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    vue(),
    vueDevTools(),
  ],
  resolve: {
    alias: {
      '@': fileURLToPath(new URL('./src', import.meta.url)),
    },
  },
  server: {
    port: 5173,
    proxy: {
      // Same-origin /api calls in dev; avoids needing CORS on the API.
      '/api': {
        target: API_URL,
        changeOrigin: true,
      },
    },
  },
})

```

```
/** Mirrors api/src/TradeBlotter.Api/Contracts/HealthResponse.cs */
export type HealthStatus = 'Healthy' | 'Degraded' | 'Unhealthy'

export interface HealthCheckEntry {
  name: string
  status: HealthStatus
  description: string | null
  durationMs: number
}

export interface HealthResponse {
  status: HealthStatus
  service: string
  version: string
  environment: string
  serverTimeUtc: string
  startedAtUtc: string
  uptimeSeconds: number
  totalDurationMs: number
  checks: HealthCheckEntry[]
}

/** The API could not be reached or did not return a health report. */
export class ApiUnreachableError extends Error {
  constructor(message: string, options?: ErrorOptions) {
    super(message, options)
    this.name = 'ApiUnreachableError'
  }
}

const REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000

/**
 * Calls GET /api/health. Resolves with the report for both 200 (Healthy/Degraded)
 * and 503 (Unhealthy); rejects with ApiUnreachableError when there is no report,
 * e.g. the API is down (the Vite proxy answers with a bare 500) or times out.
 */
export async function fetchHealth(): Promise<HealthResponse> {
  let response: Response
  try {
    response = await fetch('/api/health', {
      headers: { Accept: 'application/json' },
      signal: AbortSignal.timeout(REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS),
    })
  } catch (error) {
    const reason =
      error instanceof DOMException && error.name === 'TimeoutError'
        ? `timed out after ${REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS / 1000}s`
        : 'network error'
    throw new ApiUnreachableError(`API unreachable (${reason})`, { cause: error })
  }

  const isReport =
    (response.ok || response.status === 503) &&
    response.headers.get('content-type')?.includes('application/json')

  if (!isReport) {
    throw new ApiUnreachableError(`API unreachable (HTTP ${response.status})`)
  }

  return (await response.json()) as HealthResponse
}
```

```
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { defineStore } from 'pinia'
import { fetchHealth, type HealthResponse } from '@/api/health'

export type ApiConnectionState = 'connecting' | 'healthy' | 'degraded' | 'unhealthy' | 'offline'

const DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 10_000

const STATE_BY_STATUS: Record<HealthResponse['status'], ApiConnectionState> = {
  Healthy: 'healthy',
  Degraded: 'degraded',
  Unhealthy: 'unhealthy',
}

/** App-wide API heartbeat. Start polling once (App.vue); read it anywhere. */
export const useHealthStore = defineStore('health', () => {
  const state = ref<ApiConnectionState>('connecting')
  const report = ref<HealthResponse | null>(null)
  const error = ref<string | null>(null)
  const latencyMs = ref<number | null>(null)
  const lastCheckedAt = ref<Date | null>(null)

  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined
  let polling = false

  async function check() {
    const startedAt = performance.now()
    try {
      const result = await fetchHealth()
      report.value = result
      state.value = STATE_BY_STATUS[result.status] ?? 'unhealthy'
      latencyMs.value = Math.round(performance.now() - startedAt)
      error.value = null
    } catch (e) {
      state.value = 'offline'
      latencyMs.value = null
      error.value = e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)
    } finally {
      lastCheckedAt.value = new Date()
    }
  }

  /** Checks immediately, then every `intervalMs` after each check completes. */
  function startPolling(intervalMs = DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS) {
    if (polling) return
    polling = true

    const tick = async () => {
      await check()
      if (polling) timer = setTimeout(tick, intervalMs)
    }
    void tick()
  }

  function stopPolling() {
    polling = false
    clearTimeout(timer)
    timer = undefined
  }

  return { state, report, error, latencyMs, lastCheckedAt, check, startPolling, stopPolling }
})
```

```
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed } from 'vue'
import { RouterLink } from 'vue-router'
import { storeToRefs } from 'pinia'
import { useHealthStore, type ApiConnectionState } from '@/stores/health'

const health = useHealthStore()
const { state, latencyMs, lastCheckedAt, error } = storeToRefs(health)

const LABELS: Record<ApiConnectionState, string> = {
  connecting: 'Connecting',
  healthy: 'Healthy',
  degraded: 'Degraded',
  unhealthy: 'Unhealthy',
  offline: 'Offline',
}

const label = computed(() => LABELS[state.value])

const tooltip = computed(() => {
  const parts = [`API: ${label.value}`]
  if (error.value) parts.push(error.value)
  if (lastCheckedAt.value) parts.push(`Last checked ${lastCheckedAt.value.toLocaleTimeString()}`)
  return parts.join('\n')
})
```

```
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { storeToRefs } from 'pinia'
import ApiStatusIndicator from '@/components/ApiStatusIndicator.vue'
import { useHealthStore } from '@/stores/health'

const health = useHealthStore()
const { report, error, latencyMs, lastCheckedAt } = storeToRefs(health)

const checking = ref(false)

async function checkNow() {
  checking.value = true
  try {
    await health.check()
  } finally {
    checking.value = false
  }
}

function formatUptime(totalSeconds: number): string {
  const s = Math.floor(totalSeconds)
  const days = Math.floor(s / 86_400)
  const hours = Math.floor((s % 86_400) / 3_600)
  const minutes = Math.floor((s % 3_600) / 60)
  const seconds = s % 60
  return [days && `${days}d`, (days || hours) && `${hours}h`, `${minutes}m`, `${seconds}s`]
    .filter(Boolean)
    .join(' ')
}

function formatTimestamp(iso: string): string {
  return new Date(iso).toLocaleString()
}
</script>

<template>
  <main class="status">
    <div class="heading">
      <h1>System Status</h1>
      <ApiStatusIndicator />
      <button type="button" :disabled="checking" @click="checkNow">
        {{ checking ? 'Checking…' : 'Check now' }}
      </button>
    </div>

    <p v-if="error" class="error">{{ error }}</p>
    <p v-if="lastCheckedAt" class="muted">
      Last checked {{ lastCheckedAt.toLocaleTimeString() }}
      <template v-if="latencyMs !== null"> · round trip {{ latencyMs }} ms</template>
      <template v-if="error && report"> · showing last known report</template>
    </p>

    <template v-if="report">
      <dl class="details">
        <dt>Service</dt>
        <dd>{{ report.service }}</dd>
        <dt>Version</dt>
        <dd>{{ report.version }}</dd>
        <dt>Environment</dt>
        <dd>{{ report.environment }}</dd>
        <dt>Started</dt>
        <dd>{{ formatTimestamp(report.startedAtUtc) }}</dd>
        <dt>Uptime</dt>
        <dd>{{ formatUptime(report.uptimeSeconds) }}</dd>
        <dt>Server time</dt>
        <dd>{{ formatTimestamp(report.serverTimeUtc) }}</dd>
      </dl>

      <h2>Checks</h2>
      <table>
        <thead>

            <th>Name</th>

            <th>Description</th>
```

```
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest'
import { createPinia, setActivePinia } from 'pinia'
import { useHealthStore } from '../health'
import type { HealthResponse } from '@/api/health'

function healthReport(status: HealthResponse['status']): HealthResponse {
  return {
    status,
    service: 'TradeBlotter.Api',
    version: '1.0.0',
    environment: 'Development',
    serverTimeUtc: '2026-10-24T12:00:00Z',
    startedAtUtc: '2026-10-24T11:00:00Z',
    uptimeSeconds: 3600,
    totalDurationMs: 0.5,
    checks: [{ name: 'self', status, description: null, durationMs: 0.1 }],
  }
}

function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status: number) {
  return new Response(JSON.stringify(body), {
    status,
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json; charset=utf-8' },
  })
}

describe('health store', () => {
  const fetchMock = vi.fn<typeof fetch>()

  beforeEach(() => {
    setActivePinia(createPinia())
    vi.stubGlobal('fetch', fetchMock)
  })

  afterEach(() => {
    fetchMock.mockReset()
    vi.unstubAllGlobals()
  })

  it('starts in the connecting state', () => {
    expect(useHealthStore().state).toBe('connecting')
  })

  it('reports healthy when the API returns 200 Healthy', async () => {
    fetchMock.mockResolvedValue(jsonResponse(healthReport('Healthy'), 200))
    const store = useHealthStore()

    await store.check()

    expect(fetchMock).toHaveBeenCalledWith('/api/health', expect.anything())
    expect(store.state).toBe('healthy')
    expect(store.report?.service).toBe('TradeBlotter.Api')
    expect(store.error).toBeNull()
    expect(store.latencyMs).not.toBeNull()
    expect(store.lastCheckedAt).toBeInstanceOf(Date)
  })

  it('reports degraded when the API returns 200 Degraded', async () => {
    fetchMock.mockResolvedValue(jsonResponse(healthReport('Degraded'), 200))
    const store = useHealthStore()

    await store.check()

    expect(store.state).toBe('degraded')
  })

  it('reports unhealthy (not offline) when the API returns 503 with a report', async () => {
    fetchMock.mockResolvedValue(jsonResponse(healthReport('Unhealthy'), 503))
    const store = useHealthStore()

    await store.check()

    expect(store.state).toBe('unhealthy')
    expect(store.report?.status).toBe('Unhealthy')
  })

  it('reports offline when the dev proxy cannot reach the API', async () => {
    fetchMock.mockResolvedValue(new Response(null, { status: 500 }))
    const store = useHealthStore()

    await store.check()

    expect(store.state).toBe('offline')
    expect(store.error).toBe('API unreachable (HTTP 500)')
    expect(store.latencyMs).toBeNull()
  })

  it('reports offline on a network error and keeps the last known report', async () => {
    fetchMock.mockResolvedValueOnce(jsonResponse(healthReport('Healthy'), 200))
    fetchMock.mockRejectedValueOnce(new TypeError('Failed to fetch'))
    const store = useHealthStore()

    await store.check()
    await store.check()

    expect(store.state).toBe('offline')
    expect(store.error).toBe('API unreachable (network error)')
    expect(store.report?.status).toBe('Healthy')
  })

  it('polls on an interval until stopped', async () => {
    vi.useFakeTimers()
    try {
      fetchMock.mockImplementation(async () => jsonResponse(healthReport('Healthy'), 200))
      const store = useHealthStore()

      store.startPolling(1_000)
      store.startPolling(1_000) // second call is a no-op
      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(0)
      expect(fetchMock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)

      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(1_000)
      expect(fetchMock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)

      store.stopPolling()
      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(5_000)
      expect(fetchMock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)
    } finally {
      vi.useRealTimers()
    }
  })
})

```

Both scripts work, and the new `GET /api/health` endpoint shows in the app's header with a details page at `/status`. I started both servers with the scripts, called the endpoint directly and through the frontend's dev server, and took a headless screenshot showing "API: Healthy". The 8 unit tests, lint, type check and both builds pass. Nothing is committed yet.

**Running it** (from the repo root, in two terminals):
```powershell
.\run_api.ps1     # API on http://localhost:5035 with hot reload (-NoWatch for plain dotnet run)
.\run_app.ps1     # frontend on http://localhost:5173; runs npm install if needed (-Install to force it)
```
`run_api.ps1` runs from the `api/` folder so the .NET 8 SDK pin applies; otherwise your newer .NET 10 SDK would be used. With hot reload on, it also opens Swagger in your browser on start; I can turn that off if it gets annoying.

**Backend:**
- **Endpoint:** `HealthController.cs` serves `/api/health`. It returns status, service name, version, environment, server time, start time, uptime and a list of individual checks.
- **Built-in health checks:** The status comes from ASP.NET Core's health checks. Adding a check for a database or market data feed is one line in `Program.cs`, and it appears automatically on the endpoint and the status page.
- **Status codes:** Healthy and Degraded return `200`; Unhealthy returns `503`.
- **Sample removed:** I deleted the template's `WeatherForecast` sample now that health replaces it.

**Frontend:**
- **Proxy:** The Vite dev server forwards `/api/*` to the API, so the API doesn't need CORS settings in dev. The `API_URL` environment variable overrides the address.
- **Store:** `stores/health.ts` checks the API every 10 seconds. It distinguishes "API reachable but reporting unhealthy" from "API down" (shown as Offline).
- **Header badge:** `ApiStatusIndicator.vue` shows a coloured dot, the status and the response time. Clicking it opens `/status`.
- **Status page:** `StatusView.vue` shows the full report and the checks table, with a "Check now" button.

The rest of the Vue template's sample pages are still there, since you were happy with the frontend scaffold. Next steps could be a first commit, or starting on the trade model and blotter grid.

### User · 2026-10-24 12:29:19

> all of those also install all pacakges required if a new user downloads this repo and want to run it out of the box?

**Claude:**

Mostly, but not completely. Here's what each script handles today and the gaps I found:

- **NuGet packages (API):** Yes. `dotnet run` and `dotnet watch` restore packages automatically.
- **npm packages, fresh clone:** Yes. `run_app.ps1` installs them when `node_modules` is missing.
- **npm packages after a `git pull` that changes dependencies:** No. `node_modules` already exists, so the install is skipped and the app breaks.
- **.NET SDK version:** It can fail. `global.json` requires 8.0.422 or newer, so someone with an older .NET 8 SDK (e.g. 8.0.3xx) gets an unclear SDK error.
- **Prerequisites:** The scripts can't install the .NET 8 SDK or Node themselves. They only check that `dotnet` and `npm` exist, not their versions.
- **Running scripts:** A fresh Windows machine blocks `.ps1` scripts by default. That needs a one-time PowerShell setting or a bypass flag.

I'll fix these now and then test from a clean copy of the repo, the way a new user would get it.

<details><summary>Tool: <code>Write</code></summary>

`C:\repos\trade-blotter-application\run_app.ps1`

```
<#
.SYNOPSIS
    Runs the Trade Blotter frontend (Vue 3 + Vite) in development mode.

.DESCRIPTION
    Starts the Vite dev server on http://localhost:5173. Requests to /api are
    proxied to the API (see app/vite.config.ts), so start it with .\run_api.ps1.

    Dependencies are installed with `npm ci` (exact versions from
    package-lock.json) on first run and again whenever package-lock.json has
    changed since the last install, e.g. after a git pull.

.PARAMETER Install
    Force a clean reinstall of dependencies before starting.

.EXAMPLE
    .\run_app.ps1
.EXAMPLE
    .\run_app.ps1 -Install
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [switch]$Install
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

if (-not (Get-Command node -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) -or -not (Get-Command npm -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
    throw 'Node.js was not found on PATH. Install Node.js 24 LTS (or 22.18+): https://nodejs.org/'
}

# Mirrors "engines" in app/package.json: ^22.18.0 || >=24.12.0
$nodeVersion = [version](node --version).TrimStart('v')
$nodeSupported = ($nodeVersion.Major -eq 22 -and $nodeVersion.Minor -ge 18) -or ($nodeVersion -ge [version]'24.12.0')
if (-not $nodeSupported) {
    Write-Warning "Node.js $nodeVersion is not supported (need ^22.18.0 or >=24.12.0); the dev server may fail. Get Node.js 24 LTS from https://nodejs.org/"
}

$appDir = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'app'

Push-Location $appDir
try {
    # npm writes node_modules/.package-lock.json on every install, so a lockfile
    # newer than it means dependencies changed since the last install.
    $installMarker = 'node_modules/.package-lock.json'
    $needsInstall = $Install -or
        -not (Test-Path $installMarker) -or
        ((Get-Item 'package-lock.json').LastWriteTimeUtc -gt (Get-Item $installMarker).LastWriteTimeUtc)

    if ($needsInstall) {
        Write-Host 'Installing frontend dependencies (npm ci)...' -ForegroundColor Cyan
        npm ci
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
    }

    npm run dev
    exit $LASTEXITCODE
}
finally {
    Pop-Location
}

```

<details><summary>Tool: <code>Write</code></summary>

`C:\repos\trade-blotter-application\README.md`

````
# Trade Blotter

| Folder | Stack |
| ------ | ----- |
| `api/` | C# / ASP.NET Core Web API on .NET 8 |
| `app/` | Vue 3 (Composition API) + TypeScript + Vite, Pinia, Vue Router |

## Prerequisites

Install these once; the run scripts take care of everything else (NuGet and npm packages).

- [.NET 8 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0) (any 8.0.x; newer SDKs alone are not enough)
- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 24 LTS (or 22.18+)
- Windows PowerShell 5.1+ (built into Windows) or PowerShell 7

If Windows refuses to run the scripts ("running scripts is disabled on this system"), allow local scripts once:

```powershell
Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned
```

or run a script without changing the policy: `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\run_api.ps1`.

## Running in development

From the repo root, in two terminals:

```powershell
.\run_api.ps1   # API  -> http://localhost:5035 (Swagger at /swagger), hot reload
.\run_app.ps1   # App  -> http://localhost:5173
```

| Script | Options |
| ------ | ------- |
| `run_api.ps1` | `-NoWatch` runs without hot reload |
| `run_app.ps1` | `-Install` forces a clean `npm ci` |

`run_app.ps1` installs npm packages on first run and again whenever `package-lock.json` changes (e.g. after a pull). The dev server proxies `/api/*` to the API; set `API_URL` to point it elsewhere.

## Health

`GET /api/health` returns overall status, version, environment, uptime and individual checks
(`200` for Healthy/Degraded, `503` for Unhealthy). The app polls it every 10 seconds, shows a
status badge in the header and full details at `/status`. Register additional checks with
`AddHealthChecks()` in `api/src/TradeBlotter.Api/Program.cs`.

````

**Claude:**

Yes, now they do. I tested it from a clean copy of the repo containing only the files git would track, so no `node_modules`, `bin` or `obj`. Running `.\run_api.ps1` and `.\run_app.ps1` installed all the packages, started both servers, and the frontend reached the API with a Healthy status.

**What I changed:**
- **Frontend packages stay current:** `run_app.ps1` now uses `npm ci`, which installs the exact versions in `package-lock.json`. It reinstalls whenever the lockfile is newer than the last install, so a `git pull` that changes dependencies triggers an install automatically. I tested both cases: a plain re-run skipped the install, and a changed lockfile reinstalled.
- **Any .NET 8 SDK works:** `global.json` now accepts any 8.0.x SDK instead of requiring 8.0.422 or newer, and still picks the newest one installed.
- **Clear errors for missing tools:**
  - `run_api.ps1` stops with a download link if no .NET 8 SDK is installed. Having only .NET 9 or 10 isn't enough.
  - `run_app.ps1` warns if the Node version is older than the project supports.
- **README:** A new root `README.md` lists the prerequisites, how to run both scripts and their options, and the health endpoint.

**What a new user still has to do once:**
- **Install the tools:** The .NET 8 SDK and Node.js 24 LTS (or 22.18+). The scripts can't install these, but they now say exactly what's missing.
- **Allow scripts, if Windows blocks them:** Run `Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned`, or start a script with `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\run_api.ps1`. Your machine already allows them.

One thing I couldn't fully test: your machine already had the NuGet packages cached, so the API restore was instant. A truly new machine will download them from nuget.org on first run, which is normal and needs no extra step.

Nothing is committed yet. Want me to make the initial commit?

````
# Trade Blotter

A trade blotter application: a .NET 8 Web API and a Vue 3 frontend.

**Current state:** the project is a working scaffold. The API, the frontend, one-command dev scripts and an end-to-end
health check (API heartbeat shown in the UI) are in place. The trade domain itself (trades, blotter grid,
persistence) is not built yet. See [What I would improve or add](#what-i-would-improve-or-add).

| Folder | Contents |
| ------ | -------- |
| `api/` | C# / ASP.NET Core Web API on .NET 8 (controller-based, Swagger in dev) |
| `app/` | Vue 3 (Composition API) + TypeScript + Vite, Pinia, Vue Router, Vitest |
| `docs/` | Architecture notes and design decisions |
| `claude/` | Log of how AI (Claude Code) was used to build this project |

## How to run the project locally

### Prerequisites

Install these once; the run scripts handle everything else (NuGet and npm packages).

- [.NET 8 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0) (any 8.0.x; having only a newer SDK is not enough)
- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 24 LTS (or 22.18+)
- Windows PowerShell 5.1+ (built into Windows) or PowerShell 7

If Windows refuses to run the scripts ("running scripts is disabled on this system"), allow local scripts once:

```powershell
Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned
```

or run a script without changing the policy: `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\run_api.ps1`.

### Start the backend and frontend

From the repo root, in two terminals:

```powershell
.\run_api.ps1   # API  -> http://localhost:5035 (Swagger at /swagger), hot reload
.\run_app.ps1   # App  -> http://localhost:5173
```

Then open <http://localhost:5173>. The header badge shows the API status; click it for the full report at `/status`.

| Script | Options |
| ------ | ------- |
| `run_api.ps1` | `-NoWatch` runs without hot reload |
| `run_app.ps1` | `-Install` forces a clean `npm ci` |

`run_app.ps1` installs npm packages on first run and again whenever `package-lock.json` changes (e.g. after a pull).
`run_api.ps1` relies on `dotnet` restoring NuGet packages automatically. The Vite dev server proxies `/api/*` to the
API; set the `API_URL` environment variable to point it somewhere other than `http://localhost:5035`.

### Tests and checks

```powershell
cd app
npm run test:unit -- --run   # Vitest
npm run type-check           # vue-tsc
npm run lint                 # oxlint + eslint
npm run build                # type-check + production build

cd ../api
dotnet build
```

The API has no automated tests yet.

### Health endpoint

`GET /api/health` returns overall status, version, environment, uptime and the individual checks
(`200` for Healthy/Degraded, `503` for Unhealthy). The app polls it every 10 seconds. Register additional checks with
`AddHealthChecks()` in `api/src/TradeBlotter.Api/Program.cs` and they appear on the endpoint and the status page
automatically.

## Assumptions and design decisions

- **Separate `api/` and `app/` projects.** The backend and frontend are independent and meet only at `/api/*`.
  Details are in [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md).
- **Controllers rather than minimal APIs.** Chosen for familiar structure as the API grows. Either would work.
- **Vite proxy instead of CORS in development.** The browser only talks to `localhost:5173`, so the API needs no CORS
  configuration for local work. CORS will need configuring if the frontend is ever hosted on a different origin.
- **Health built on ASP.NET Core health checks.** The controller aggregates the registered checks into one JSON
  document. Only Unhealthy returns `503`; Degraded still serves traffic and returns `200`.
- **The UI distinguishes "unhealthy" from "offline".** A `503` with a report means the API is up but reporting a problem.
  No report at all (network error, timeout, or a proxy error page) means offline.
- **Polling, not push, for status.** A self-scheduling timer in a Pinia store checks every 10 seconds.
  This is simple and good enough for
````

````
# Architecture

## Overview

```
Browser ──► Vite dev server :5173 ──(proxy /api/*)──► ASP.NET Core API :5035
            serves the Vue app                         controllers + health checks
```

The repository has two independent projects that meet only at HTTP endpoints under `/api`.

### `api/`

```
api/
├── global.json                      # pins the .NET 8 SDK line
├── TradeBlotter.sln
└── src/TradeBlotter.Api/
    ├── Program.cs                   # service registration and pipeline
    ├── Controllers/HealthController.cs
    └── Contracts/HealthResponse.cs  # response shapes (records)
```

- Controller-based Web API on .NET 8, with Swagger UI in development.
- `Contracts/` holds the types that cross the wire, kept separate from future domain types.

### `app/`

```
app/src/
├── api/health.ts                    # fetch wrapper and response types
├── stores/health.ts                 # Pinia store: polling and connection state
├── components/ApiStatusIndicator.vue
├── views/StatusView.vue             # /status details page
├── router/index.ts
└── App.vue                          # starts polling, shows the header badge
```

Data flows one way: `api/` function → Pinia store → components. Components read store state and never call `fetch`
themselves.

## Health feature end to end

1. `Program.cs` registers checks with `AddHealthChecks()` (currently a single `self` check).
2. `GET /api/health` runs `HealthCheckService`, then maps the report to `HealthResponse`.
   Healthy and Degraded return `200`; Unhealthy returns `503`. The body is JSON in both cases.
3. `api/health.ts` returns the report for `200` and `503`, and throws `ApiUnreachableError` when there is no report
   (network error, 5-second timeout, or a non-JSON response such as the Vite proxy's plain-text `502`).
4. `stores/health.ts` maps the result to a connection state: `connecting`, `healthy`, `degraded`, `unhealthy` or
   `offline`. It polls every 10 seconds and keeps the last known report when a later check fails.
5. `ApiStatusIndicator.vue` (header badge) and `StatusView.vue` (details table) render that state.

`HealthResponse` is mirrored by hand in `app/src/api/health.ts`. Changing one means changing the other until the
types are generated from OpenAPI (see the README's improvement list).

## Environments

| | Development |
| --- | --- |
| API | `http://localhost:5035` (the `http` launch profile), run with `dotnet watch` |
| Frontend | `http://localhost:5173`; `/api` proxied to the API (override with `API_URL`) |
| Other environments | Not defined yet: no hosting, CORS or configuration decisions have been made |

````

```
# Design decisions

Short records of choices that shape the project. Newest at the bottom.

## 1. Two independent projects: `api/` and `app/`

**Decision:** A .NET 8 Web API and a Vue 3 (Composition API) frontend in separate folders, joined only by HTTP.
**Why:** Matches the requested structure and lets each side be built, tested and deployed on its own.
**Trade-off:** Types are duplicated across the boundary until they are generated from OpenAPI.

## 2. Vite proxy for `/api` in development

**Decision:** The dev server forwards `/api/*` to `http://localhost:5035`; the API has no CORS configuration.
**Why:** The browser sees a single origin, so local development needs no CORS setup and no hard-coded API URL in
frontend code.
**Trade-off:** Only covers dev. Hosting the frontend on another origin later requires CORS or a reverse proxy.

## 3. Health endpoint aggregates ASP.NET Core health checks

**Decision:** `HealthController` calls `HealthCheckService` and returns a custom JSON report. Unhealthy is `503`;
Degraded stays `200`.
**Why:** New dependencies (database, market data) become one registration line and appear in the report with no
controller changes. Degraded still serves traffic, so load balancers should not treat it as down.
**Trade-off:** One endpoint serves both "is the process up" and "are dependencies healthy". A production setup would
likely split liveness and readiness.

## 4. The UI separates "unhealthy" from "offline"

**Decision:** A `503` carrying a report is `unhealthy`. No report (network error, timeout, non-JSON response) is `offline`.
**Why:** "The API told us something is wrong" and "we cannot reach the API" need different responses from a user.
**Found by testing:** with the API stopped, the Vite proxy returns a plain-text `502`, not a `500` as first assumed.
The client therefore keys on the response having a JSON health body, not on a particular status code.

## 5. Polling with a self-scheduling timer

**Decision:** The Pinia store schedules the next check only after the previous one finishes, every 10 seconds.
**Why:** Checks can never overlap or pile up behind a slow response. Simpler than a push channel for a heartbeat.
**Trade-off:** Up to 10 seconds of lag in the badge. Live trade data would use SignalR or SSE instead.

## 6. Reproducible setup

**Decision:** `run_app.ps1` uses `npm ci` and reinstalls when `package-lock.json` is newer than `node_modules`.
`api/global.json` pins SDK `8.0.100` with `rollForward: latestFeature`.
**Why:** A fresh clone runs with two commands, and a pull that changes dependencies does not leave a stale
`node_modules`. Any installed 8.0.x SDK is accepted, but a newer major SDK alone is not.
**Trade-off:** The scripts cannot install .NET or Node themselves; they check for them and say what is missing.

## 7. Windows PowerShell dev scripts

**Decision:** `run_api.ps1` and `run_app.ps1` at the repo root.
**Why:** The requested workflow and the author's platform.
**Trade-off:** Not usable as-is on macOS or Linux without PowerShell 7. The underlying commands are
`dotnet watch run` and `npm run dev`.

```

```
- Record what was verified by running it, separately from what was only read or assumed.
- Record places where the output was wrong, changed or rejected. That is the most useful information here.
- The **Author review** lines in the log are for the project author to fill in. Claude cannot know what you
```

```
namespace TradeBlotter.Api.Domain;

public enum TradeSide
{
    Buy,
    Sell,
}

/// <summary>An executed equity trade. Trades are immutable once booked.</summary>
public sealed class Trade
{
    public long Id { get; init; }

    /// <summary>Ticker, stored upper-case (e.g. AAPL).</summary>
    public required string Symbol { get; init; }

    public TradeSide Side { get; init; }

    /// <summary>Number of shares; always positive. Direction comes from <see cref="Side"/>.</summary>
    public int Quantity { get; init; }

    /// <summary>Price per share; always positive.</summary>
    public decimal Price { get; init; }

    /// <summary>When the trade was booked (UTC), set by the server.</summary>
    public DateTimeOffset Timestamp { get; init; }

    /// <summary>Quantity signed by side: positive for Buy, negative for Sell.</summary>
    public long SignedQuantity => Side == TradeSide.Buy ? Quantity : -(long)Quantity;
}

```

```
namespace TradeBlotter.Api.Domain;

/// <summary>
/// Derives positions from trades using the weighted average cost method.
/// </summary>
/// <remarks>
/// Trades are replayed per symbol in booking order:
/// <list type="bullet">
/// <item>Opening or adding to a position (same direction): average cost becomes the
/// quantity-weighted average of the existing position and the new trade.</item>
/// <item>Reducing a position (opposite direction): average cost is unchanged; selling
/// part of a long does not change what the remaining shares cost.</item>
/// <item>Closing to exactly zero: the position is flat and dropped from the result.</item>
/// <item>Flipping through zero (e.g. long 100, sell 150): the old position closes and the
/// remainder opens a new one at this trade's price.</item>
/// </list>
/// Short positions (negative quantity) are allowed and mirror the long rules.
/// </remarks>
public static class PositionCalculator
{
    public static IReadOnlyList<Position> Calculate(IEnumerable<Trade> trades)
    {
        var books = new Dictionary<string, (long Quantity, decimal AverageCost)>(StringComparer.Ordinal);

        foreach (var trade in trades.OrderBy(t => t.Timestamp).ThenBy(t => t.Id))
        {
            var current = books.GetValueOrDefault(trade.Symbol);
            books[trade.Symbol] = Apply(current.Quantity, current.AverageCost, trade.SignedQuantity, trade.Price);
        }

        return books
            .Where(b => b.Value.Quantity != 0)
            .OrderBy(b => b.Key, StringComparer.Ordinal)
            .Select(b => new Position(b.Key, b.Value.Quantity, b.Value.AverageCost))
            .ToList();
    }

    private static (long Quantity, decimal AverageCost) Apply(
        long quantity, decimal averageCost, long tradeQuantity, decimal price)
    {
        var newQuantity = quantity + tradeQuantity;

        // Opening or adding in the same direction: weighted average.
        if (quantity == 0 || Math.Sign(quantity) == Math.Sign(tradeQuantity))
        {
            var totalCost = Math.Abs(quantity) * averageCost + Math.Abs(tradeQuantity) * price;
            return (newQuantity, totalCost / Math.Abs(newQuantity));
        }

        // Closed flat.
        if (newQuantity == 0)
        {
            return (0, 0m);
        }

        // Partially reduced: remaining shares keep their cost.
        if (Math.Sign(newQuantity) == Math.Sign(quantity))
        {
            return (newQuantity, averageCost);
        }

        // Flipped through zero: the remainder is a new position opened at this price.
        return (newQuantity, price);
    }
}

```

```
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Storage.ValueConversion;
using TradeBlotter.Api.Domain;

namespace TradeBlotter.Api.Data;

public sealed class TradeBlotterDbContext(DbContextOptions<TradeBlotterDbContext> options) : DbContext(options)
{
    public DbSet<Trade> Trades => Set<Trade>();

    protected override void OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder modelBuilder)
    {
        var trade = modelBuilder.Entity<Trade>();

        trade.HasKey(t => t.Id);
        trade.Property(t => t.Symbol).HasMaxLength(12).IsRequired();
        trade.Property(t => t.Side).HasConversion<string>().HasMaxLength(4);

        // SQLite cannot ORDER BY a DateTimeOffset stored as text; store it as a sortable integer.
        trade.Property(t => t.Timestamp).HasConversion(new DateTimeOffsetToBinaryConverter());
        trade.HasIndex(t => t.Timestamp);

        trade.Ignore(t => t.SignedQuantity);
    }
}

```

```
using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations;
using TradeBlotter.Api.Domain;

namespace TradeBlotter.Api.Contracts;

/// <summary>Body of <c>POST /api/trades</c>. The server assigns the id and timestamp.</summary>
/// <remarks>Properties are nullable so a missing field reports "required" rather than defaulting to 0.</remarks>
public sealed record CreateTradeRequest
{
    [Required]
    [RegularExpression(@"^\s*[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9.\-]{0,11}\s*$",
        ErrorMessage = "Symbol must start with a letter and be at most 12 letters, digits, '.' or '-'.")]
    public string? Symbol { get; init; }

    [Required]
    public TradeSide? Side { get; init; }

    [Required]
    [Range(1, int.MaxValue, ErrorMessage = "Quantity must be a positive whole number of shares.")]
    public int? Quantity { get; init; }

    [Required]
    [Range(0.0001, 1_000_000_000, ErrorMessage = "Price must be greater than 0.")]
    public decimal? Price { get; init; }
}

public sealed record TradeResponse(
    long Id,
    string Symbol,
    TradeSide Side,
    int Quantity,
    decimal Price,
    decimal Notional,
    DateTimeOffset Timestamp)
{
    public static TradeResponse From(Trade trade) => new(
        trade.Id,
        trade.Symbol,
        trade.Side,
        trade.Quantity,
        trade.Price,
        trade.Quantity * trade.Price,
        trade.Timestamp);
}

```

```
public sealed class TradesController(
    TradeBlotterDbContext db,
    IHubContext<TradesHub, ITradesClient> hub,
    TimeProvider timeProvider) : ControllerBase
{
    /// <summary>All trades, newest first.</summary>
    [HttpGet]
    [ProducesResponseType<IReadOnlyList<TradeResponse>>(StatusCodes.Status200OK)]
    public async Task<IReadOnlyList<TradeResponse>> GetAll(CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        var trades = await db.Trades
            .AsNoTracking()
            .OrderByDescending(t => t.Timestamp)
            .ThenByDescending(t => t.Id)
            .ToListAsync(cancellationToken);

        return trades.Select(TradeResponse.From).ToList();
    }

    [HttpGet("{id:long}")]
    [ProducesResponseType<TradeResponse>(StatusCodes.Status200OK)]
    [ProducesResponseType(StatusCodes.Status404NotFound)]
    public async Task<ActionResult<TradeResponse>> GetById(long id, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        var trade = await db.Trades.AsNoTracking().FirstOrDefaultAsync(t => t.Id == id, cancellationToken);
        return trade is null ? NotFound() : TradeResponse.From(trade);
    }

    /// <summary>Books a trade and broadcasts it to live blotters.</summary>
    [HttpPost]
    [Consumes("application/json")]
    [ProducesResponseType<TradeResponse>(StatusCodes.Status201Created)]
    [ProducesResponseType<ValidationProblemDetails>(StatusCodes.Status400BadRequest)]
    public async Task<ActionResult<TradeResponse>> Create(
        CreateTradeRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        // [ApiController] has already rejected invalid requests with 400, so the values are present.
        var trade = new Trade
        {
            Symbol = request.Symbol!.Trim().ToUpperInvariant(),
            Side = request.Side!.Value,
            Quantity = request.Quantity!.Value,
            Price = request.Price!.Value,
            Timestamp = timeProvider.GetUtcNow(),
        };

        db.Trades.Add(trade);
        await db.SaveChangesAsync(cancellationToken);

        var response = TradeResponse.From(trade);
        await hub.Clients.All.TradeAdded(response);

        return CreatedAtAction(nameof(GetById), new { id = trade.Id }, response);
    }
}
```

```
using System.Text.Json.Serialization;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Diagnostics.HealthChecks;
using TradeBlotter.Api.Data;
using TradeBlotter.Api.Hubs;

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

// Add services to the container.

// Enums travel as names ("Buy"/"Sell"), and numeric values are rejected.
var enumConverter = new JsonStringEnumConverter(allowIntegerValues: false);

builder.Services.AddControllers()
    .AddJsonOptions(o => o.JsonSerializerOptions.Converters.Add(enumConverter));
builder.Services.AddSignalR()
    .AddJsonProtocol(o => o.PayloadSerializerOptions.Converters.Add(enumConverter));

// Learn more about configuring Swagger/OpenAPI at https://aka.ms/aspnetcore/swashbuckle
builder.Services.AddEndpointsApiExplorer();
builder.Services.AddSwaggerGen();

builder.Services.AddSingleton(TimeProvider.System);

builder.Services.AddDbContext<TradeBlotterDbContext>(o =>
    o.UseSqlite(builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("TradeBlotter")));

// Register dependency checks here; they are aggregated by GET /api/health.
builder.Services.AddHealthChecks()
    .AddCheck("self", () => HealthCheckResult.Healthy("API process is running"))
    .AddDbContextCheck<TradeBlotterDbContext>("database");

var app = builder.Build();

// Create or upgrade the SQLite database on startup so a fresh clone runs with no setup step.
using (var scope = app.Services.CreateScope())
{
    scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<TradeBlotterDbContext>().Database.Migrate();
}

// Configure the HTTP request pipeline.
if (app.Environment.IsDevelopment())
{
    app.UseSwagger();
    app.UseSwaggerUI();
}

app.UseHttpsRedirection();

app.UseAuthorization();

app.MapControllers();
app.MapHub<TradesHub>("/hubs/trades");

app.Run();

// Exposed for WebApplicationFactory in integration tests.
public partial class Program;
```

```
using TradeBlotter.Api.Domain;
using static TradeBlotter.Api.Domain.TradeSide;

namespace TradeBlotter.Api.Tests;

public class PositionCalculatorTests
{
    private static readonly DateTimeOffset Start = new(2026, 10, 24, 9, 30, 0, TimeSpan.Zero);
    private static long _nextId;

    /// <summary>Builds a trade booked <paramref name="minute"/> minutes after the open.</summary>
    private static Trade T(string symbol, TradeSide side, int quantity, decimal price, int minute) => new()
    {
        Id = Interlocked.Increment(ref _nextId),
        Symbol = symbol,
        Side = side,
        Quantity = quantity,
        Price = price,
        Timestamp = Start.AddMinutes(minute),
    };

    [Fact]
    public void No_trades_gives_no_positions()
    {
        Assert.Empty(PositionCalculator.Calculate([]));
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Single_buy_opens_long_at_trade_price()
    {
        var positions = PositionCalculator.Calculate([T("AAPL", Buy, 100, 150m, 0)]);

        Assert.Equal([new Position("AAPL", 100, 150m)], positions);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Buys_average_by_quantity_weight()
    {
        // (100 * 10 + 50 * 13) / 150 = 11
        var positions = PositionCalculator.Calculate(
        [
            T("AAPL", Buy, 100, 10m, 0),
            T("AAPL", Buy, 50, 13m, 1),
        ]);

        Assert.Equal([new Position("AAPL", 150, 11m)], positions);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Partial_sell_reduces_quantity_and_keeps_average_cost()
    {
        // Avg after buys: (100 * 10 + 100 * 20) / 200 = 15; selling at any price leaves the rest at 15.
        var positions = PositionCalculator.Calculate(
        [
            T("AAPL", Buy, 100, 10m, 0),
            T("AAPL", Buy, 100, 20m, 1),
            T("AAPL", Sell, 50, 30m, 2),
        ]);

        Assert.Equal([new Position("AAPL", 150, 15m)], positions);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Buy_after_partial_sell_averages_with_remaining_cost()
    {
        // Hold 50 @ 10 after the sell; add 50 @ 20 -> (50 * 10 + 50 * 20) / 100 = 15
        var positions = PositionCalculator.Calculate(
        [
            T("AAPL", Buy, 100, 10m, 0),
            T("AAPL", Sell, 50, 12m, 1),
            T("AAPL", Buy, 50, 20m, 2),
        ]);

        Assert.Equal([new Position("AAPL", 100, 15m)], positions);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Flat_position_is_omitted()
    {
        var positions = PositionCalculator.Calculate(
        [
            T("AAPL", Buy, 100, 10m, 0),
            T("AAPL", Sell, 100, 12m, 1),
        ]);

        Assert.Empty(positions);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Reopening_after_flat_starts_a_fresh_average()
    {
        var positions = PositionCalculator.Calculate(
        [
            T("AAPL", Buy, 100, 10m, 0),
            T("AAPL", Sell, 100, 12m, 1),
            T("AAPL", Buy, 10, 50m, 2),
        ]);

        Assert.Equal([new Position("AAPL", 10, 50m)], positions);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Selling_through_zero_flips_to_short_at_the_flipping_trade_price()

        // Long 100 closes; the extra 50 opens a short at 12.
        var positions = PositionCalculator.Calculate(
        [
            T("AAPL", Buy, 100, 10m, 0),
            T("AAPL", Sell, 150, 12m, 1),
        ]);

        Assert.Equal([new Position("AAPL", -50, 12m)], positions);
    }

        // Short 200 @ (100 * 20 + 100 * 10) / 200 = 15; buying 50 back leaves short 150 @ 15.

        [
            T("MSFT", Sell, 100, 20m, 0),
            T("MSFT", Sell, 100, 10m, 1),
            T("MSFT", Buy, 50, 5m, 2),

        Assert.Equal([new Position("MSFT", -150, 15m)], positions);
```

```
/** Mirrors api/src/TradeBlotter.Api/Contracts/TradeContracts.cs and Domain/Position.cs */
export type TradeSide = 'Buy' | 'Sell'

export interface Trade {
  id: number
  symbol: string
  side: TradeSide
  quantity: number
  price: number
  notional: number
  /** ISO 8601, UTC, assigned by the server. */
  timestamp: string
}

export interface NewTrade {
  symbol: string
  side: TradeSide
  quantity: number
  price: number
}

export interface Position {
  symbol: string
  /** Positive is long, negative is short. */
  netQuantity: number
  averageCost: number
}

/** A 400 from the API, with messages keyed by request field (symbol, side, quantity, price). */
export class TradeRejectedError extends Error {
  constructor(
    message: string,
    readonly fieldErrors: Record<string, string>,
  ) {
    super(message)
    this.name = 'TradeRejectedError'
  }
}

async function getJson<T>(url: string): Promise<T> {
  const response = await fetch(url, { headers: { Accept: 'application/json' } })
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`GET ${url} failed (HTTP ${response.status})`)
  }
  return (await response.json()) as T
}

export function fetchTrades(): Promise<Trade[]> {
  return getJson<Trade[]>('/api/trades')
}

export function fetchPositions(): Promise<Position[]> {
  return getJson<Position[]>('/api/positions')
}

export async function createTrade(trade: NewTrade): Promise<Trade> {
  const response = await fetch('/api/trades', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', Accept: 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify(trade),
  })

  if (response.status === 400) {
    // ASP.NET ValidationProblemDetails: { title, errors: { Quantity: ["..."] } }
    const problem = (await response.json().catch(() => ({}))) as {
      title?: string
      errors?: Record<string, string[]>
    }
    const fieldErrors: Record<string, string> = {}
    for (const [key, messages] of Object.entries(problem.errors ?? {})) {
      const field = key.replace(/^\$\.?/, '').toLowerCase() || 'form'
      fieldErrors[field] = messages[0] ?? 'Invalid value.'
    }
    throw new TradeRejectedError(problem.title ?? 'The trade was rejected.', fieldErrors)
  }

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Could not book the trade (HTTP ${response.status}).`)
  }

  return (await response.json()) as Trade
}
```

```
import { HubConnectionBuilder, LogLevel, type HubConnection } from '@microsoft/signalr'
import type { Trade } from './trades'

/** Server-to-client messages on /hubs/trades (see api/.../Hubs/TradesHub.cs). */
export interface TradesHubHandlers {
  tradeAdded(trade: Trade): void
}

export function createTradesConnection(handlers: TradesHubHandlers): HubConnection {
  const connection = new HubConnectionBuilder()
    .withUrl('/hubs/trades')
    .withAutomaticReconnect()
    .configureLogging(LogLevel.Warning)
    .build()

  connection.on('TradeAdded', handlers.tradeAdded)
  return connection
}

```

```
import type { NewTrade, TradeSide } from '@/api/trades'

/** Raw form input: numbers stay strings until validated so "" and "abc" can be reported. */
export interface TradeForm {
  symbol: string
  side: TradeSide | ''
  quantity: string
  price: string
}

export type TradeFormErrors = Partial<Record<keyof TradeForm, string>>

export type TradeValidation =
  | { ok: true; trade: NewTrade }
  | { ok: false; errors: TradeFormErrors }

// Same rules as CreateTradeRequest on the API.
const SYMBOL_PATTERN = /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9.-]{0,11}$/
const MAX_QUANTITY = 2_147_483_647
const MAX_PRICE = 1_000_000_000

export function validateTrade(form: TradeForm): TradeValidation {
  const errors: TradeFormErrors = {}

  const symbol = form.symbol.trim().toUpperCase()
  if (!symbol) {
    errors.symbol = 'Enter a symbol.'
  } else if (!SYMBOL_PATTERN.test(symbol)) {
    errors.symbol = 'Letters, digits, "." or "-", starting with a letter (max 12).'
  }

  if (!form.side) {
    errors.side = 'Choose Buy or Sell.'
  }

  const quantityText = form.quantity.trim()
  const quantity = Number(quantityText)
  if (!quantityText) {
    errors.quantity = 'Enter a quantity.'
  } else if (!Number.isInteger(quantity) || quantity <= 0) {
    errors.quantity = 'Quantity must be a positive whole number.'
  } else if (quantity > MAX_QUANTITY) {
    errors.quantity = 'Quantity is too large.'
  }

  const priceText = form.price.trim()
  const price = Number(priceText)
  if (!priceText) {
    errors.price = 'Enter a price.'
  } else if (!Number.isFinite(price) || price <= 0) {
    errors.price = 'Price must be greater than 0.'
  } else if (price > MAX_PRICE) {
    errors.price = 'Price is too large.'
  }

  if (Object.keys(errors).length > 0) {
    return { ok: false, errors }
  }

  return { ok: true, trade: { symbol, side: form.side as TradeSide, quantity, price } }
}
```

```
const quantityFormat = new Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, { maximumFractionDigits: 0 })
const priceFormat = new Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, {
  minimumFractionDigits: 2,
  maximumFractionDigits: 4,
})
const amountFormat = new Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, {
  minimumFractionDigits: 2,
  maximumFractionDigits: 2,
})
const timeFormat = new Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, {
  hour: '2-digit',
  minute: '2-digit',
  second: '2-digit',
  hour12: false,
})
const dateFormat = new Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, { month: 'short', day: 'numeric' })

export const formatQuantity = (value: number) => quantityFormat.format(value)
export const formatPrice = (value: number) => priceFormat.format(value)
export const formatAmount = (value: number) => amountFormat.format(value)

/** Time only for today's trades; date and time otherwise. */
export function formatTimestamp(iso: string, now = new Date()): string {
  const date = new Date(iso)
  const time = timeFormat.format(date)
  return date.toDateString() === now.toDateString() ? time : `${dateFormat.format(date)} ${time}`
}
```

```
import { computed, ref } from 'vue'
import { defineStore } from 'pinia'
import { HubConnectionState, type HubConnection } from '@microsoft/signalr'
import {
  createTrade,
  fetchPositions,
  fetchTrades,
  type NewTrade,
  type Position,
  type Trade,
} from '@/api/trades'
import { createTradesConnection } from '@/api/tradesHub'

export type LiveFeedState = 'connecting' | 'live' | 'reconnecting' | 'offline'

const RECONNECT_DELAY_MS = 5_000
const NEW_TRADE_HIGHLIGHT_MS = 2_500

const newestFirst = (a: Trade, b: Trade) =>
  Date.parse(b.timestamp) - Date.parse(a.timestamp) || b.id - a.id

/**
 * Trades, positions and the live feed. Trades arrive from three places: the initial
 * load, this browser's own submissions, and SignalR broadcasts (which include this
 * browser's submissions too), so every path goes through upsertTrade to stay de-duplicated.
 */
export const useBlotterStore = defineStore('blotter', () => {
  const trades = ref<Trade[]>([])
  const positions = ref<Position[]>([])
  const loading = ref(false)
  const loadError = ref<string | null>(null)
  const liveState = ref<LiveFeedState>('connecting')
  /** Trades that arrived after the initial load, briefly highlighted in the blotter. */
  const newTradeIds = ref(new Set<number>())

  const tradeCount = computed(() => trades.value.length)

  let connection: HubConnection | undefined
  let reconnectTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined
  let positionsRequest = 0

  function upsertTrade(trade: Trade, highlight: boolean) {
    if (trades.value.some((t) => t.id === trade.id)) return

    trades.value = [...trades.value, trade].sort(newestFirst)
    if (highlight) {
      newTradeIds.value.add(trade.id)
      setTimeout(() => newTradeIds.value.delete(trade.id), NEW_TRADE_HIGHLIGHT_MS)
    }
  }

  /** Positions are derived on the server; re-fetch after any trade. Late responses are ignored. */
  async function refreshPositions() {
    const request = ++positionsRequest
    const latest = await fetchPositions()
    if (request === positionsRequest) positions.value = latest
  }

  async function load() {
    loading.value = true
    try {
      const [loadedTrades] = await Promise.all([fetchTrades(), refreshPositions()])
      trades.value = loadedTrades.sort(newestFirst)
      loadError.value = null
    } catch (e) {
      loadError.value = e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)
    } finally {
      loading.value = false
    }
  }

  async function submitTrade(trade: NewTrade): Promise<Trade> {
    const booked = await createTrade(trade)
    // Show it immediately rather than waiting for the broadcast (which may be down).
    upsertTrade(booked, true)
    void refreshPositions().catch(() => {})
    return booked
  }

  function onTradeAdded(trade: Trade) {
    upsertTrade(trade, true)
    void refreshPositions().catch(() => {})
  }

  async function connect() {
    clearTimeout(reconnectTimer)
    if (!connection) {
      connection = createTradesConnection({ tradeAdded: onTradeAdded })
      connection.onreconnecting(() => (liveState.value = 'reconnecting'))
      // Missed broadcasts while disconnected: reload everything.
      connection.onreconnected(() => {
        liveState.value = 'live'
        void load()
      })
      // Automatic reconnect gave up: keep retrying on our own schedule.
      connection.onclose(() => {
        if (!connection) return
        liveState.value = 'offline'
        reconnectTimer = setTimeout(connect, RECONNECT_DELAY_MS)
      })
    }

    if (connection.state !== HubConnectionState.Disconnected) return

    liveState.value = 'connecting'
    try {
      await connection.start()
      liveState.value = 'live'
      void load()
    } catch {
      // API not reachable yet (initial start is not covered by automatic reconnect).
      liveState.value = 'offline'
      reconnectTimer = setTimeout(connect, RECONNECT_DELAY_MS)
    }
  }

  /** Load data and open the live feed. Call once from the app shell. */
  function start
… (362 more characters)
```

```
const submitting = ref(false)
const lastBooked = ref<Trade | null>(null)
let lastBookedTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined

const errors = computed<TradeFormErrors>(() => ({
  ...serverErrors.value,
  ...(showErrors.value && !validation.value.ok ? validation.value.errors : {}),
}))

// Server feedback is about the values that were sent; drop it once they change.
watch(form, () => {
  serverErrors.value = {}
  formError.value = null
})

const notional = computed(() => {
  const quantity = Number(form.quantity)
  const price = Number(form.price)
  return form.quantity && form.price && quantity > 0 && price > 0 ? quantity * price : null
})

const submitLabel = computed(() => {
  if (submitting.value) return 'Booking…'
  if (!validation.value.ok) return form.side || 'Submit'
  const { side, quantity, symbol, price } = validation.value.trade
  return `${side} ${formatQuantity(quantity)} ${symbol} @ ${formatPrice(price)}`
})

async function onSubmit() {
  showErrors.value = true
  const result = validation.value
  if (!result.ok || submitting.value) return

  submitting.value = true
  try {
    const booked = await blotter.submitTrade(result.trade)

    lastBooked.value = booked
    clearTimeout(lastBookedTimer)
    lastBookedTimer = setTimeout(() => (lastBooked.value = null), 4_000)

    // Fresh ticket; keep the side, since consecutive trades often go the same way.
    Object.assign(form, { symbol: '', quantity: '', price: '' })
    showErrors.value = false
    symbolInput.value?.focus()
  } catch (e) {
    if (e instanceof TradeRejectedError && Object.keys(e.fieldErrors).length > 0) {
      serverErrors.value = e.fieldErrors
    } else {
      formError.value = e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)
    }
  } finally {
    submitting.value = false
  }
}
</script>

<template>
  <form class="card ticket" novalidate @submit.prevent="onSubmit">
    <h2 class="card-title">New trade</h2>

    <div class="fields">
      <fieldset class="side" :class="form.side.toLowerCase()">
```

```
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, ref } from 'vue'
import { storeToRefs } from 'pinia'
import type { Trade } from '@/api/trades'
import { useBlotterStore } from '@/stores/blotter'
import { formatAmount, formatPrice, formatQuantity, formatTimestamp } from '@/utils/format'

type SortKey = 'timestamp' | 'symbol' | 'side' | 'quantity' | 'price' | 'notional'
type SortDirection = 'asc' | 'desc'

interface Column {
  key: SortKey
  label: string
  numeric?: boolean
  /** Direction used the first time the column is clicked. */
  firstDirection: SortDirection
}

const columns: Column[] = [
  { key: 'timestamp', label: 'Time', firstDirection: 'desc' },
  { key: 'symbol', label: 'Symbol', firstDirection: 'asc' },
  { key: 'side', label: 'Side', firstDirection: 'asc' },
  { key: 'quantity', label: 'Quantity', numeric: true, firstDirection: 'desc' },
  { key: 'price', label: 'Price', numeric: true, firstDirection: 'desc' },
  { key: 'notional', label: 'Notional', numeric: true, firstDirection: 'desc' },
]

const blotter = useBlotterStore()
const { trades, newTradeIds, loading } = storeToRefs(blotter)

const sortKey = ref<SortKey>('timestamp')
const sortDirection = ref<SortDirection>('desc')

function sortBy(column: Column) {
  if (sortKey.value === column.key) {
    sortDirection.value = sortDirection.value === 'asc' ? 'desc' : 'asc'
  } else {
    sortKey.value = column.key
    sortDirection.value = column.firstDirection
  }
}

function compare(a: Trade, b: Trade, key: SortKey): number {
  switch (key) {
    case 'timestamp':
      return Date.parse(a.timestamp) - Date.parse(b.timestamp) || a.id - b.id
    case 'symbol':
    case 'side':
      return a[key].localeCompare(b[key])
    default:
      return a[key] - b[key]
  }
}

const sortedTrades = computed(() => {
  const sign = sortDirection.value === 'asc' ? 1 : -1
  // Ties fall back to newest first so equal values stay in a predictable order.
  return [...trades.value].sort(
    (a, b) => sign * compare(a, b, sortKey.value) || compare(b, a, 'timestamp'),
  )
})

function ariaSort(column: Column) {
  if (sortKey.value !== column.key) return 'none'
  return sortDirection.value === 'asc' ? 'ascending' : 'descending'
}
</script>

<template>
  <section class="card blotter">
    <h2 class="card-title">
      <span>Blotter</span>
      <span class="count">{{ trades.length }} {{ trades.length === 1 ? 'trade' : 'trades' }}</span>
    </h2>

    <div class="scroll">
      <table>
        <thead>
          <tr>
            <th
              v-for="column in columns"
              :key="column.key"
              :class="{ num: column.numeric }"
              :aria-sort="ariaSort(column)"
            >
              <button type="button" class="sort" @click="sortBy(column)">
                {{ column.label }}
                <span class="arrow" aria-hidden="true">
                  {{ sortKey === column.key ? (sortDirection === 'asc' ? '▲' : '▼') : '' }}
                </span>
              </button>
            </th>
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr
            v-for="trade in sortedTrades"
            :key="trade.id"
            :class="[trade.side.toLowerCase(), { new: newTradeIds.has(trade.id) }]"
          >
            <td class="time" :title="new Date(trade.timestamp).toLocaleString()">
              {{ formatTimestamp(trade.timestamp) }}
            </td>
            <td class="symbol">{{ trade.symbol }}</td>
            <td>
              <span class="side-badge" :class="trade.side.toLowerCase()">{{ trade.side }}</span>
            </td>
            <td class="num">{{ formatQuantity(trade.quantity) }}</td>
            <td class="num">{{ formatPrice(trade.price) }}</td>
            <td class="num">{{ formatAmount(trade.notional) }}</td>
          </tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>

      <p v-if="trades.length === 0" class="empty">
        {{ loading ? 'Loading trades…' : 'No trades yet. Book one with the ticket.' }}
      </p>
    </div>
  </sec
```

```
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
import { validateTrade, type TradeForm } from '../validateTrade'

const valid: TradeForm = { symbol: 'aapl ', side: 'Buy', quantity: '100', price: '150.25' }

describe('validateTrade', () => {
  it('normalizes a valid ticket', () => {
    expect(validateTrade(valid)).toEqual({
      ok: true,
      trade: { symbol: 'AAPL', side: 'Buy', quantity: 100, price: 150.25 },
    })
  })

  it('reports every empty field', () => {
    const result = validateTrade({ symbol: ' ', side: '', quantity: '', price: '' })

    expect(result.ok).toBe(false)
    if (!result.ok) {
      expect(Object.keys(result.errors).sort()).toEqual(['price', 'quantity', 'side', 'symbol'])
    }
  })

  it.each([
    ['0', 'positive'],
    ['-5', 'positive'],
    ['1.5', 'whole'],
    ['abc', 'whole'],
  ])('rejects quantity %s', (quantity, message) => {
    const result = validateTrade({ ...valid, quantity })

    expect(result.ok).toBe(false)
    if (!result.ok) expect(result.errors.quantity).toContain(message)
  })

  it.each(['0', '-1', 'abc'])('rejects price %s', (price) => {
    const result = validateTrade({ ...valid, price })

    expect(result.ok).toBe(false)
    if (!result.ok) expect(result.errors.price).toBe('Price must be greater than 0.')
  })

  it.each(['1AAPL', 'AA PL', 'TOOLONGSYMBOL'])('rejects symbol %s', (symbol) => {
    expect(validateTrade({ ...valid, symbol }).ok).toBe(false)
  })

  it('accepts share-class symbols', () => {
    expect(validateTrade({ ...valid, symbol: 'brk.b' }).ok).toBe(true)
  })
})
```

```
  it('loads trades newest first along with positions', async () => {
    api.fetchTrades.mockResolvedValue([trade(1, 0), trade(2, 5), trade(3, 2)])
    api.fetchPositions.mockResolvedValue([aaplPosition])
    const store = useBlotterStore()

    await store.load()

    expect(store.trades.map((t) => t.id)).toEqual([2, 3, 1])
    expect(store.positions).toEqual([aaplPosition])
    expect(store.loadError).toBeNull()
  })

  it('shows a submitted trade once even though the broadcast echoes it back', async () => {
    const booked = trade(7, 10)
    api.createTrade.mockResolvedValue(booked)
    api.fetchPositions.mockResolvedValue([aaplPosition])
    const store = useBlotterStore()
    store.start()
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(hub.tradeAdded).toBeDefined())

    await store.submitTrade({ symbol: 'AAPL', side: 'Buy', quantity: 10, price: 100 })
    hub.tradeAdded!(booked)

    expect(store.trades.filter((t) => t.id === 7)).toHaveLength(1)
    expect(store.newTradeIds.has(7)).toBe(true)
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(store.positions).toEqual([aaplPosition]))
  })

  it('adds trades broadcast by other users in time order and refreshes positions', async () => {
    api.fetchTrades.mockResolvedValue([trade(1, 0)])
    const store = useBlotterStore()
    store.start()
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(store.trades).toHaveLength(1))
    api.fetchPositions.mockResolvedValue([aaplPosition])

    hub.tradeAdded!(trade(2, 30, 'MSFT'))

    expect(store.trades.map((t) => t.id)).toEqual([2, 1])
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(store.positions).toEqual([aaplPosition]))
  })

  it('reports a load failure', async () => {
    api.fetchTrades.mockRejectedValue(new Error('GET /api/trades failed (HTTP 502)'))
    const store = useBlotterStore()

    await store.load()

    expect(store.loadError).toBe('GET /api/trades failed (HTTP 502)')
    expect(store.loading).toBe(false)
  })
})

```
```
import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
import { mount } from '@vue/test-utils'
import { createPinia, setActivePinia } from 'pinia'
import type { Trade } from '@/api/trades'
import { useBlotterStore } from '@/stores/blotter'
import BlotterTable from '../BlotterTable.vue'

function trade(id: number, symbol: string, side: Trade['side'], minute: number): Trade {
  return {
    id,
    symbol,
    side,
    quantity: 10,
    price: 1,
    notional: 10,
    timestamp: new Date(Date.UTC(2026, 9, 24, 14, minute)).toISOString(),
  }
}

describe('BlotterTable', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    const pinia = createPinia()
    setActivePinia(pinia)
    useBlotterStore().trades = [
      trade(1, 'MSFT', 'Buy', 0),
      trade(2, 'AAPL', 'Sell', 5),
      trade(3, 'TSLA', 'Buy', 2),
    ]
  })

  const symbols = (wrapper: ReturnType<typeof mount>) =>
    wrapper.findAll('tbody td.symbol').map((td) => td.text())

  it('shows newest trades first by default', () => {
    const wrapper = mount(BlotterTable)

    expect(symbols(wrapper)).toEqual(['AAPL', 'TSLA', 'MSFT'])
    expect(wrapper.find('th[aria-sort="descending"]').text()).toContain('Time')
  })

  it('sorts by a column on click and reverses on a second click', async () => {
    const wrapper = mount(BlotterTable)
    const symbolHeader = wrapper.findAll('th button').find((b) => b.text().startsWith('Symbol'))!

    await symbolHeader.trigger('click')
    expect(symbols(wrapper)).toEqual(['AAPL', 'MSFT', 'TSLA'])

    await symbolHeader.trigger('click')
    expect(symbols(wrapper)).toEqual(['TSLA', 'MSFT', 'AAPL'])
  })

  it('marks each row and badge with its side', () => {
    const wrapper = mount(BlotterTable)
    const rows = wrapper.findAll('tbody tr')

    expect(rows[0]!.classes()).toContain('sell')
    expect(rows[0]!.find('.side-badge').text()).toBe('Sell')
    expect(rows[1]!.classes()).toContain('buy')
  })
})
```

```
// End-to-end check through the Vite dev proxy: SignalR broadcast + REST contract.
const appDir = process.argv[2]
const signalR = require(require.resolve('@microsoft/signalr', { paths: [appDir] }))
const base = 'http://localhost:5173'

async function post(body) {
  const r = await fetch(`${base}/api/trades`, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  })
  return { status: r.status, location: r.headers.get('location'), body: await r.json() }
}

;(async () => {
  const received = []
  const conn = new signalR.HubConnectionBuilder()
    .withUrl(`${base}/hubs/trades`)
    .configureLogging(signalR.LogLevel.Warning)
    .build()
  conn.on('TradeAdded', (t) => received.push(t))
  await conn.start()
  console.log('hub connected via proxy, transport:', conn.connection.transport.constructor.name)

  const trades = [
    { symbol: 'aapl', side: 'Buy', quantity: 100, price: 150 },
    { symbol: 'AAPL', side: 'Buy', quantity: 50, price: 156 },
    { symbol: 'AAPL', side: 'Sell', quantity: 30, price: 160 },
    { symbol: 'MSFT', side: 'Buy', quantity: 20, price: 410.5 },
    { symbol: 'TSLA', side: 'Sell', quantity: 15, price: 220.25 },
    { symbol: 'NVDA', side: 'Buy', quantity: 40, price: 120 },
    { symbol: 'NVDA', side: 'Sell', quantity: 40, price: 125 },
  ]
  for (const t of trades) {
    const r = await post(t)
    console.log('POST', r.status, r.location, r.body.symbol, r.body.side, r.body.notional)
  }

  const bad = await post({ symbol: '', side: 'Hold', quantity: 0, price: -1 })
  console.log('POST invalid ->', bad.status, JSON.stringify(bad.body.errors))

  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 500))
  console.log('broadcasts received:', received.length, 'of', trades.length)

  const positions = await (await fetch(`${base}/api/positions`)).json()
  console.log('positions:', JSON.stringify(positions))
  const list = await (await fetch(`${base}/api/trades`)).json()
  console.log('trades newest first:', list.map((t) => t.id).join(','))
  await conn.stop()
})().catch((e) => {
  console.error('FAILED', e)
  process.exit(1)
})

```

```
import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest'
import { flushPromises, mount } from '@vue/test-utils'
import { createPinia, setActivePinia } from 'pinia'
import { TradeRejectedError, type Trade } from '@/api/trades'
import { useBlotterStore } from '@/stores/blotter'
import TradeEntryForm from '../TradeEntryForm.vue'

const booked: Trade = {
  id: 1,
  symbol: 'AAPL',
  side: 'Sell',
  quantity: 100,
  price: 150.25,
  notional: 15025,
  timestamp: '2026-10-24T14:00:00Z',
}

describe('TradeEntryForm', () => {
  let submitTrade: ReturnType<typeof vi.spyOn>

  beforeEach(() => {
    setActivePinia(createPinia())
    submitTrade = vi.spyOn(useBlotterStore(), 'submitTrade').mockResolvedValue(booked)
  })

  async function fill(wrapper: ReturnType<typeof mount>, symbol: string, qty: string, px: string) {
    await wrapper.find('#trade-symbol').setValue(symbol)
    await wrapper.find('#trade-quantity').setValue(qty)
    await wrapper.find('#trade-price').setValue(px)
  }

  it('shows field errors only after a submit attempt, and does not submit', async () => {
    const wrapper = mount(TradeEntryForm)
    expect(wrapper.findAll('.field-error')).toHaveLength(0)

    await wrapper.find('form').trigger('submit')

    expect(wrapper.findAll('.field-error').map((e) => e.text())).toEqual([
      'Enter a symbol.',
      'Enter a quantity.',
      'Enter a price.',
    ])
    expect(submitTrade).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
  })

  it('submits a normalized trade, then clears the ticket but keeps the side', async () => {
    const wrapper = mount(TradeEntryForm)
    await wrapper.find('input[value="Sell"]').setValue(true)
    await fill(wrapper, ' aapl', '100', '150.25')

    expect(wrapper.find('button[type="submit"]').text()).toMatch(/^Sell 100 AAPL @ 150\.25$/)
    await wrapper.find('form').trigger('submit')
    await flushPromises()

    expect(submitTrade).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
      symbol: 'AAPL',
      side: 'Sell',
      quantity: 100,
      price: 150.25,
    })
    expect((wrapper.find('#trade-symbol').element as HTMLInputElement).value).toBe('')
    expect((wrapper.find('input[value="Sell"]').element as HTMLInputElement).checked).toBe(true)
    expect(wrapper.find('.booked').text()).toContain('Booked sell 100 AAPL')
  })

  it('shows server-side field errors next to the field', async () => {
    submitTrade.mockRejectedValue(
      new TradeRejectedError('Validation failed', { price: 'Price must be greater than 0.' }),
    )
    const wrapper = mount(TradeEntryForm)
    await fill(wrapper, 'AAPL', '10', '5')

    await wrapper.find('form').trigger('submit')
    await flushPromises()

    expect(wrapper.find('#trade-price-error').text()).toBe('Price must be greater than 0.')
  })
})

```

````
# Trade Blotter

Enter equity trades, watch them appear in a live blotter, and see current positions (net quantity and average cost)
derived from the trade history. Built for the exercise in [docs/trade-blotter-exercise.docx](docs/trade-blotter-exercise.docx).

| Folder | Contents |
| ------ | -------- |
| `api/` | C# / ASP.NET Core Web API on .NET 8: EF Core + SQLite, SignalR, xUnit tests |
| `app/` | Vue 3 (Composition API) + TypeScript + Vite, Pinia, Vitest |
| `docs/` | Exercise brief, architecture notes, design decisions |
| `claude/` | How AI (Claude Code) was used, including the session transcript |

## How to run the project locally

### Prerequisites

Install these once; the run scripts handle everything else (NuGet and npm packages, and the database).

- [.NET 8 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0) (any 8.0.x; having only a newer SDK is not enough)
- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 24 LTS (or 22.18+)
- Windows PowerShell 5.1+ (built into Windows) or PowerShell 7

If Windows refuses to run the scripts ("running scripts is disabled on this system"), allow local scripts once:

```powershell
Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned
```

or run a script without changing the policy: `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\run_api.ps1`.

### Start the backend and frontend

From the repo root, in two terminals:

```powershell
.\run_api.ps1   # API  -> http://localhost:5035 (Swagger at /swagger), hot reload
.\run_app.ps1   # App  -> http://localhost:5173
```

Open <http://localhost:5173> and book a trade. Open a second browser window to see trades arrive live.

| Script | Options |
| ------ | ------- |
| `run_api.ps1` | `-NoWatch` runs without hot reload |
| `run_app.ps1` | `-Install` forces a clean `npm ci` |

- The SQLite database (`api/src/TradeBlotter.Api/trade-blotter.db`) is created and migrated automatically on API
  startup. Delete the file to start from an empty blotter.
- `run_app.ps1` installs npm packages on first run and again whenever `package-lock.json` changes.
- Without PowerShell, the equivalent commands are `dotnet watch run --project src/TradeBlotter.Api --launch-profile http`
  from `api/`, and `npm ci && npm run dev` from `app/`.

### Tests and checks

```powershell
cd api
dotnet test                   # xUnit: position calculation + API integration tests

cd ../app
npm run test:unit -- --run    # Vitest: validation, store, components
npm run type-check            # vue-tsc
npm run lint                  # oxlint + eslint
npm run build                 # type-check + production build
```

## API

| Method | Path | Result |
| ------ | ---- | ------ |
| `POST` | `/api/trades` | Books a trade. `201 Created` with the trade and a `Location` header; `400` with per-field errors |
| `GET` | `/api/trades` | All trades, newest first |
| `GET` | `/api/trades/{id}` | One trade, or `404` |
| `GET` | `/api/positions` | Open positions per symbol (`netQuantity`, `averageCost`); flat symbols omitted |
| `GET` | `/api/health` | Status of the API and database (`200`, or `503` if unhealthy) |
| WS | `/hubs/trades` | SignalR: pushes `TradeAdded` to every connected blotter |

```json
// POST /api/trades
{ "symbol": "AAPL", "side": "Buy", "quantity": 100, "price": 150.25 }

// 201 Created
{ "id": 1, "symbol": "AAPL", "side": "Buy", "quantity": 100, "price": 150.25,
  "notional": 15025.00, "timestamp": "2026-10-24T13:00:00+00:00" }

// GET /api/positions
[{ "symbol": "AAPL", "netQuantity": 100, "averageCost": 150.25 }]
```

Swagger UI at <http://localhost:5035/swagger> documents the same contracts, and `TradeBlotter.Api.http` has ready-made
requests.
````
