Fair point, and it's fixed. Every clickable control in the app now shows the hand cursor.

The main culprit was **Buy/Sell**, the control you use most. Each one is a hidden radio button laid over the visible button. The visible button already had the hand cursor, but the invisible radio on top of it showed the default arrow, and that's what the mouse was actually over.

**What changed:**
- **Buy/Sell:** the hidden radio now shows the hand cursor itself.
- **Global rule** in `main.css`: buttons, links, radio and checkbox controls, and anything marked as a button get the hand cursor automatically, so new components can't miss it. Disabled buttons show a "not allowed" cursor, except the submit button, which shows the busy cursor while a trade is booking.

**Checked in a real browser:** on the Blotter, Positions and Status pages, I found the element at the centre of every clickable control and read its cursor. All 36 controls (16, 12 and 8) show the pointer, including the ticket's **Use** button after typing KO. The 52 tests and lint still pass.

```
# Marks & anatomy
The quiet, considered look is a few fixed specs plus two pieces of negative space.
The data is the only thing allowed to be loud.
## Mark specs (fixed across every chart)
| Mark | Spec |
|---|---|
| Bar / column | **<= 24px thick** (cap it - never fill the slot; let the band's leftover be air); **4px rounded data-end, square at the baseline**; grows from a single baseline |
| Line | **2px**, round join/cap |
| Marker / end-dot | **>= 8px** (r >= 4), filled with the series color |
| Area fill | the series hue at **~10% opacity** (a wash, never a saturated block) |
| Gridlines / axes | one-step-off-surface gray, **hairline (1px), solid** (never dashed), recessive |
## The two spacers (white doing the separating)
- **Surface gap.** A **2px gap** in the surface color separates touching marks - every
  segment of a stacked bar, and every adjacent (touching) bar, the same width. Keep it
  one consistent width across a stack; neighbors one step apart read distinct because of
  the gap, not a stroke drawn around them.
- **Surface ring.** Dots and end-markers carry a **2px ring in the surface color**,
  so they stay legible where they cross a line or overlap each other. The ring is part
  of the mark's hover/hit target, not just spacing - see `interaction.md` (small dots
  are easy to under-size for hover).
Never draw a border around a mark to separate it. The gap and the ring are the
mechanism; a stroke adds data-weight ink that isn't data.
## Labels & legend
A **legend is always present for two or more series** - the dependable identity
channel; never make the reader rely on color-matching alone. Direct labels then ride
the marks to *supplement* it. **A single series needs no legend box**: there is only
one color, so the chart's title or subtitle already says what is plotted. A box with
one swatch restates the title and costs space.
- **Label selectively - never a number on every point.** A value beside every dot or
  segment is chaos and goes unread. Label the endpoint, the extreme, or the one series
  the story is about; let the axis, the legend, and the tooltip/table carry the rest.
  Direct labels work *because* they are sparing - flood the chart and they stop working.
- **Direct labels before gridlines; gridlines before a second axis.**
- **A label that won't fit doesn't get clipped - measure first.** Only place a label
  *inside* a bar or stacked segment when the rendered text fits with comfortable
  padding on both sides. If it doesn't fi
… (3515 more characters)
```

```
# Interaction - tooltips & filters
An HTML chart is interactive by default - the hover layer is part of the deliverable,
not an upgrade. Omitting it is the exception (a bare stat tile), never the default.
Design it with the same care as the static render.
## Tooltips & hover
Tooltips **enhance, they never gate**: every value a tooltip shows is also reachable
without it, through direct labels or the table view. Same details on keyboard focus
as on hover.
- **The crosshair finds the X.** A vertical hairline tracks the pointer and snaps to
  the nearest data position. Readers aim at a date, never at a 2px line.
- **On bars and cells, the mark is the hit target.** No crosshair - each bar, segment,
  dot, or heat-cell carries its own `pointermove`/`focus` tooltip showing category and
  value, and the hovered mark lifts (slight lighten or outline) so the reader sees it respond.
- **One tooltip, every series.** The readout lists every series at that X - the
  pointer never has to land on a line or a fill to get a value.
- **Labels are untrusted data - use `textContent`.** Series and category names
  often come from CSV headers, tool output, or API responses. Insert them into
  tooltip/legend/table DOM with `textContent` or `createTextNode`, never via
  `innerHTML` string concatenation.
- **Values lead, labels follow.** In the tooltip the value is the Strong,
  high-contrast element and the series name is secondary - the legend's hierarchy
  inverted, because here the reader has the series and wants the number.
- **Line keys, not boxes.** Tooltip rows key their series with a short stroke of the
  series color; at tooltip density a filled box is data-weight ink doing a label's
  job. (Legends still mirror the mark: rect for bars/areas, line for lines.)
- **The hit target is bigger than the mark.** A mark's hover/focus area includes its
  2px surface gap and then some - never only the painted pixels. An 8px scatter dot is a
  pinpoint nobody hits reliably; give each point a transparent hit area of at least
  **24px**, or - for dense scatter - a nearest-point / Voronoi layer so the pointer only
  has to be *closest*, not dead-center. (The crosshair already does this for the X on
  line and bar charts; scatter and bubble need the per-point version.)
- **A value pushed off its mark lives in the tooltip.** When a label won't fit inside a
  small bar (see `marks-and-anatomy.md`), that bar's hit area carries the value on hover
  and focus - the tooltip is its overflow hom
```

```bash
  low52w: 'LOW_52WEEK',
  beta: 'EQY_BETA',
  avgVolume30d: 'VOLUME_AVG_30D',
} as const

const TEXT_FIELDS = new Set(['name', 'sector', 'industry', 'currency', 'exDividendDate'])

/** Fundamentals change slowly: let DeskLink's cache serve them for an hour. */
const PROFILE_CACHE_SECONDS = 3600

async function postDeskLink<T>(path: string, body: unknown, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<T> {
  let response: Response
  try {
    response = await fetch(`${DESKLINK_URL}${path}`, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify(body),
      signal,
    })
  } catch (e) {
    if (e instanceof DOMException && e.name === 'AbortError') throw e
    throw new LivePriceUnavailableError('DeskLink is not reachable from this page')
  }
  const envelope = (await response.json().catch(() => null)) as {
    ok: boolean
    error?: string
    data?: T
  } | null
  if (!envelope?.ok || envelope.data === undefined) {
    throw new LivePriceUnavailableError(envelope?.error ?? `DeskLink error (HTTP ${response.status})`)
  }
  return envelope.data
}

/** The DES-style fields for one symbol, or null when Bloomberg does not know it. */
export async function fetchSecurityProfile(
  symbol: string,
  signal?: AbortSignal,
): Promise<SecurityProfile | null> {
  const security = toBloombergSecurity(symbol)
  const data = await postDeskLink<NonNullable<BdpEnvelope['data']>>(
    '/con/bloomberg/bdp',
    {
      securities: [security],
      fields: Object.values(PROFILE_FIELDS),
      mode: 'auto',
      ttlSeconds: PROFILE_CACHE_SECONDS,
    },
    signal,
  )

  const raw = data.data?.[security]
  if (!raw || raw.NAME == null) return null

  const profile = {} as Record<string, string | number | null>
  for (const [key, field] of Object.entries(PROFILE_FIELDS)) {
    const value = raw[field] ?? null
    if (TEXT_FIELDS.has(key)) {
      profile[key] = value
    } else {
      const n = Number(value)
      profile[key] = value === null || !Number.isFinite(n) ? null : n
    }
  }
  return profile as unknown as SecurityProfile
}
```

```
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, onBeforeUnmount, onMounted, ref, useTemplateRef } from 'vue'
import type { PricePoint } from '@/api/bloomberg'
import type { TradeSide } from '@/api/trades'
import { formatPrice, formatQuantity, formatSignedPercent } from '@/utils/format'

export interface ChartTrade {
  /** YYYY-MM-DD, New York trading date. */
  date: string
  side: TradeSide
  quantity: number
  price: number
}

const props = defineProps<{
  symbol: string
  points: PricePoint[]
  averageCost: number | null
  trades: ChartTrade[]
}>()

const RANGES = [1, 2, 3, 5] as const
const years = ref<(typeof RANGES)[number]>(1)

// ---------- size ----------
const HEIGHT = 220
const M = { top: 12, right: 58, bottom: 24, left: 8 }
const frame = useTemplateRef<HTMLDivElement>('frame')
const width = ref(640)
let observer: ResizeObserver | undefined
onMounted(() => {
  if (!frame.value) return
  observer = new ResizeObserver(([entry]) => {
    if (entry) width.value = Math.max(280, Math.round(entry.contentRect.width))
  })
  observer.observe(frame.value)
})
onBeforeUnmount(() => observer?.disconnect())

// ---------- data in range ----------
const visible = computed(() => {
  const last = props.points.at(-1)
```

```
  averageCost: number
  last: number | null
}>()

const profile = ref<SecurityProfile | null>(null)
const profileState = ref<'loading' | 'ready' | 'not-found' | 'unavailable'>('loading')
const history = ref<PricePoint[]>([])
const historyState = ref<'loading' | 'ready' | 'unavailable'>('loading')

const controller = new AbortController()
onBeforeUnmount(() => controller.abort())

onMounted(() => {
  fetchSecurityProfile(props.symbol, controller.signal)
    .then((p) => {
      profile.value = p
      profileState.value = p ? 'ready' : 'not-found'
    })
    .catch(() => {
      if (!controller.signal.aborted) profileState.value = 'unavailable'
    })

  fetchPriceHistory(props.symbol)
    .then((points) => {
      history.value = points
      historyState.value = 'ready'
    })
    .catch(() => (historyState.value = 'unavailable'))
})

// Trades for this symbol, dated by the New York session they were booked in.

  trades.value

      quantity: t.quantity,
      price: t.price,
    })),
)

const compact = new Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, { notation: 'compact', maximumFractionDigits: 1 })
const two = (v: number | null) => (v === null ? '—' : v.toFixed(2))
const ratio = (v: number | null) => (v === null ? '—' : `${v.toFixed(1)}x`)
const pct = (v: number | null) => (v === null ? '—' : `${v.toFixed(2)}%`)

/** Where the last price sits in the 52-week range, 0 to 100. */

  return Math.min(100, Math.max(0, ((props.last - p.low52w) / (p.high52w - p.low52w)) * 100))
})
```

```
      dayPnl: previousClose === null ? null : p.netQuantity * (quote.last - previousClose),

/** Totals over any set of valued rows (e.g. the filtered rows on screen). */
export function summarize(rows: ValuedPosition[]): PortfolioTotals {
  const sum = (
    pick: (r: ValuedPosition) => number | null,
    where: (r: ValuedPosition) => boolean = () => true,
  ) => rows.filter(where).reduce((total, r) => total + (pick(r) ?? 0), 0)

  const longMarketValue = sum(
    (r) => r.marketValue,
    (r) => r.netQuantity > 0,
  )
  const shortMarketValue = sum(
    (r) => r.marketValue,
    (r) => r.netQuantity < 0,
  )

  return {
    positions: rows.length,
    longs: rows.filter((r) => r.netQuantity > 0).length,
    shorts: rows.filter((r) => r.netQuantity < 0).length,
    priced: rows.filter((r) => r.last !== null).length,
    longMarketValue,
    shortMarketValue,
    netExposure: longMarketValue + shortMarketValue,
    grossExposure: longMarketValue - shortMarketValue,
    unrealizedPnl: sum((r) => r.unrealizedPnl),
    dayPnl: sum((r) => r.dayPnl),
  }


}
```

```bash
function sortBy(key: SortKey | null) {
```

```
    if (key === 'symbol') return sign * a.symbol.localeCompare(b.symbol)
    // Unpriced rows sink to the bottom whichever way the column is sorted.
    const x = a[key]
    const y = b[key]
    if (x === null || y === null) return x === y ? 0 : x === null ? 1 : -1
    return sign * (x - y) || a.symbol.localeCompare(b.symbol)
  })
})

const totals = computed(() => summarize(filtered.value))

// ---------- expandable rows ----------
const expanded = ref(new Set<string>())

function toggle(symbol: string) {
  if (expanded.value.has(symbol)) expanded.value.delete(symbol)
  else expanded.value.add(symbol)
}
```

```
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, ref } from 'vue'
import { storeToRefs } from 'pinia'
import type { Trade } from '@/api/trades'
import { useBlotterStore } from '@/stores/blotter'
import { formatAmount, formatPrice, formatQuantity, formatTimestamp } from '@/utils/format'

type SortKey = 'timestamp' | 'symbol' | 'side' | 'quantity' | 'price' | 'notional'
type SortDirection = 'asc' | 'desc'

interface Column {
  key: SortKey
  label: string
  numeric?: boolean
  /** Direction used the first time the column is clicked. */
  firstDirection: SortDirection
}

const columns: Column[] = [
  { key: 'timestamp', label: 'Time', firstDirection: 'desc' },
  { key: 'symbol', label: 'Symbol', firstDirection: 'asc' },
  { key: 'side', label: 'Side', firstDirection: 'asc' },
  { key: 'quantity', label: 'Quantity', numeric: true, firstDirection: 'desc' },
  { key: 'price', label: 'Price', numeric: true, firstDirection: 'desc' },
  { key: 'notional', label: 'Notional', numeric: true, firstDirection: 'desc' },
]

const blotter = useBlotterStore()
const { trades, newTradeIds, loading } = storeToRefs(blotter)

const sortKey = ref<SortKey>('timestamp')
const sortDirection = ref<SortDirection>('desc')

function sortBy(column: Column) {
  if (sortKey.value === column.key) {
    sortDirection.value = sortDirection.value === 'asc' ? 'desc' : 'asc'
  } else {
    sortKey.value = column.key
    sortDirection.value = column.firstDirection
  }
}

function compare(a: Trade, b: Trade, key: SortKey): number {
  switch (key) {
    case 'timestamp':
      return Date.parse(a.timestamp) - Date.parse(b.timestamp) || a.id - b.id
    case 'symbol':
    case 'side':
      return a[key].localeCompare(b[key])
    default:
      return a[key] - b[key]
  }
}

const sortedTrades = computed(() => {
  const sign = sortDirection.value === 'asc' ? 1 : -1
  // Ties fall back to newest first so equal values stay in a predictable order.
  return [...trades.value].sort(
    (a, b) => sign * compare(a, b, sortKey.value) || compare(b, a, 'timestamp'),
  )
})

function ariaSort(column: Column) {
  if (sortKey.value !== column.key) return 'none'
  return sortDirection.value === 'asc' ? 'ascending' : 'descending'
}
</script>
```

```
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
import { mount } from '@vue/test-utils'
import type { PricePoint } from '@/api/bloomberg'
import PriceHistoryChart from '../PriceHistoryChart.vue'

/** One close per weekday from `from`, rising by 1 a day from 100. */
function series(from: string, days: number): PricePoint[] {
  const points: PricePoint[] = []
  const d = new Date(`${from}T00:00:00Z`)
  while (points.length < days) {
    if (d.getUTCDay() % 6 !== 0) {
      points.push({ date: d.toISOString().slice(0, 10), close: 100 + points.length })
    }
    d.setUTCDate(d.getUTCDate() + 1)
  }
  return points
}

const points = series('2021-10-25', 1300) // a little over five years

function mountChart(trades = [] as { date: string; side: 'Buy' | 'Sell'; quantity: number; price: number }[]) {
  return mount(PriceHistoryChart, {
    props: { symbol: 'KO', points, averageCost: 1200, trades },
  })
}

describe('PriceHistoryChart', () => {
  it('shows one year by default and widens to five', async () => {
    const wrapper = mountChart()
    const oneYear = wrapper.find('.summary').text()

    await wrapper.findAll('.ranges button').find((b) => b.text() === '5Y')!.trigger('click')
    const fiveYears = wrapper.find('.summary').text()

    expect(wrapper.find('.ranges button[aria-pressed="true"]').text()).toBe('5Y')
    expect(oneYear).not.toEqual(fiveYears)
    // The 5Y window starts five years before the last close.
    const last = points.at(-1)!.date
    expect(fiveYears).toContain(String(Number(last.slice(0, 4)) - 5))
  })

  it('draws the average cost line and a ▲/▼ marker per trade in range', () => {
    const inRange = points.at(-10)!.date
    const outOfRange = points[0]!.date // older than the default 1Y window
    const wrapper = mountChart([
      { date: inRange, side: 'Buy', quantity: 10, price: 1290 },
      { date: inRange, side: 'Sell', quantity: 5, price: 1291 },
      { date: outOfRange, side: 'Buy', quantity: 1, price: 100 },
    ])

    expect(wrapper.find('.avg text').text()).toContain('1,200.00')
    expect(wrapper.findAll('.marker.buy')).toHaveLength(1)
    expect(wrapper.findAll('.marker.sell')).toHaveLength(1)
  })

  it('reads values with the keyboard, including the trades on that day', async () => {
    const last = points.at(-1)!
    const wrapper = mountChart([{ date: last.date, side: 'Sell', quantity: 7, price: 1399 }])
    const frame = wrapper.find('.frame')

    await frame.trigger('keydown', { key: 'End' })
    expect(wrapper.find('.tooltip').text()).toContain(last.close.toLocaleString(undefined, { minimumFractionDigits: 2 }))
    expect(wrapper.find('.tooltip').text()).toContain('Sell 7')

    await frame.trigger('keydown', { key: 'ArrowLeft' })
    expect(wrapper.find('.tooltip').text()).not.toContain('Sell 7')

    await frame.trigger('keydown', { key: 'Escape' })
    expect(wrapper.find('.tooltip').exists()).toBe(false)
  })
})

```
```
import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest'
import { flushPromises, mount } from '@vue/test-utils'
import { createPinia, setActivePinia } from 'pinia'
import type { LiveQuote, PricePoint, SecurityProfile } from '@/api/bloomberg'
import { useBlotterStore } from '@/stores/blotter'
import PositionsView from '../PositionsView.vue'

const bloomberg = vi.hoisted(() => ({
  fetchLiveQuotes: vi.fn<(symbols: string[]) => Promise<Map<string, LiveQuote>>>(),
  fetchSecurityProfile: vi.fn<(symbol: string) => Promise<SecurityProfile | null>>(),
  fetchPriceHistory: vi.fn<(symbol: string) => Promise<PricePoint[]>>(),
}))
vi.mock('@/api/bloomberg', () => bloomberg)

const quote = (symbol: string, last: number): LiveQuote => ({
  symbol,
  name: `${symbol} CORP`,
  last,
  changePercent: null,
  asOf: '2026-10-24T13:35:16Z',
})

describe('PositionsView', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    setActivePinia(createPinia())
    useBlotterStore().positions = [
      { symbol: 'KO', netQuantity: -100, averageCost: 90 }, // short, price fell: gainer
      { symbol: 'PEP', netQuantity: 100, averageCost: 140 }, // long, price fell: loser
      { symbol: 'WMT', netQuantity: 50, averageCost: 100 }, // long, price rose: gainer
    ]
    bloomberg.fetchLiveQuotes.mockResolvedValue(
      new Map([
        ['KO', quote('KO', 85)],
        ['PEP', quote('PEP', 130)],
        ['WMT', quote('WMT', 110)],
      ]),
    )
    bloomberg.fetchSecurityProfile.mockResolvedValue(null)
    bloomberg.fetchPriceHistory.mockResolvedValue([])
  })

  const symbols = (wrapper: ReturnType<typeof mount>) =>
    wrapper.findAll('tr.position-row .symbol').map((td) => td.text())
  const chip = (wrapper: ReturnType<typeof mount>, label: string) =>
    wrapper.findAll('.quick-filter button').find((b) => b.text() === label)!

  it('filters by direction and P&L, and the totals follow the filter', async () => {
    const wrapper = mount(PositionsView)
    await flushPromises()
    expect(symbols(wrapper)).toEqual(['KO', 'PEP', 'WMT'])

    await chip(wrapper, 'Long').trigger('click')
    expect(symbols(wrapper)).toEqual(['PEP', 'WMT'])

    await chip(wrapper, 'Gainers').trigger('click')
    expect(symbols(wrapper)).toEqual(['WMT'])
    expect(wrapper.find('.filter-count').text()).toContain('Showing 1 of 3')
    expect(wrapper.find('tfoot').text()).toContain('+500.00') // WMT only: (110 − 100) × 50

    await wrapper.find('.filter-clear').trigger('click')
    expect(symbols(wrapper)).toEqual(['KO', 'PEP', 'WMT'])
  })

  it('searches by symbol or name', async () => {
    const wrapper = mount(PositionsView)
    await flushPromises()

    await wrapper.find('.filter-search').setValue('pep corp')
    expect(symbols(wrapper)).toEqual(['PEP'])
  })

  it('expands a row into its detail panel and collapses it again', async () => {
    const wrapper = mount(PositionsView)
    await flushPromises()
    const toggle = wrapper.find('tr.position-row button.expand')

    await toggle.trigger('click')
    await flushPromises()
    expect(toggle.attributes('aria-expanded')).toBe('true')
    expect(wrapper.find('.detail-row').exists()).toBe(true)
    expect(bloomberg.fetchSecurityProfile).toHaveBeenCalledWith('KO', expect.anything())
    expect(bloomberg.fetchPriceHistory).toHaveBeenCalledWith('KO')

    await toggle.trigger('click')
    expect(wrapper.find('.detail-row').exists()).toBe(false)
  })
})
```

### User · 2026-10-24 13:56:26

> sorry man but I figure I have to do this why in trade.cs is only symbol required?

**Claude:**

It's inconsistent, and the reason isn't a domain reason.

`Symbol` has `required` only because it's a non-nullable `string`. Without it, the compiler warns that the property could be left null (CS8618), and `required` was the quick way to silence that warning. The other properties are value types (`TradeSide`, `int`, `decimal`, `DateTimeOffset`), which have defaults, so the compiler never complained about them. That's the gap. This compiles without a warning:

```csharp
var trade = new Trade { Symbol = "AAPL" };   // Side = Buy, Quantity = 0, Price = 0, Timestamp = 0001-01-01
```

That's a meaningless trade, and the domain type allows it. Today it can't actually happen through the app, for three reasons:

- `CreateTradeRequest` validates every field: `[Required]`, positive quantity, positive price, and `Buy`/`Sell` only.
- The controller and the seeder set all the properties.
- The database columns are `NOT NULL`.

So the safety lives at the edges, not in the type itself. Given the brief grades whether Trade is a clean, well-reasoned type, that's worth fixing. Two options:

1. **Make everything `required` except `Id`.** `Id` is assigned by the database. The compiler then forces whoever creates a trade to set side, quantity, price and timestamp. Every place that creates one already does, so it's a one-line change per property. EF Core 8 still loads trades from the database fine with `required` properties.
2. **Option 1, plus enforce the rules inside `Trade`.** A constructor or `Trade.Create(...)` would reject a quantity or price of zero or less, an empty or malformed symbol, and a timestamp that isn't UTC. Then an invalid `Trade` can't exist at all, wherever it's created from, instead of relying on the request validation.

I'd do option 2. The API's validation stays as it is, giving users friendly 400 errors per field, while the domain type guarantees the rules underneath. I'd add a few unit tests showing it rejects bad values.

Want me to go ahead with option 2?

### User · 2026-10-24 13:58:24

> I understand option 2 I agre mostly but what is someone does a buy for -200 that is just short 200...

**Claude:**

Good question. Here's why I'd still reject a negative quantity: **"Buy −200" doesn't mean "short 200". If it means anything, it means "sell 200".** Being short is a position you end up in, not a kind of trade. You get short 200 by *selling* 200 shares you don't own. Selling 200 when flat leaves you at −200, and the positions page then shows "Short".

Accepting a signed quantity alongside a side causes two problems:

- **Two ways to say the same thing.** "Buy −200" and "Sell 200" would book the identical trade, so every report, filter and total has to normalize them. For example, filtering "Buy" would quietly include what are really sells.
- **Contradictory tickets.** "Sell −200" would mean buying 200. A trader who fat-fingers a minus sign gets the *opposite* of what the Side button says, which is the worst kind of error on a blotter.

That's why real order protocols like FIX carry quantity as always positive and put direction only in the side. They even have a separate **"Sell Short"** side, because regulators care whether a sale opens a short (Reg SHO borrow/locate rules), even though the position maths is the same as a sell.

So: quantity positive, direction from the side. I can make the trader's intent clearer in two ways:

1. **Show the resulting position in the ticket.** It would read something like "KO: −285 → −485 (short)", or "flat → −200 (short)". The trader sees they're opening or adding to a short before booking. The positions are already in the store, so this is cheap, and I think it's what you're really after.
2. **Optionally, add a Sell Short side.** It would be booked like a Sell, but labelled SHORT on the blotter, so short sales stand out. It's more realistic, but more change. The brief only asks for Buy/Sell, so I'd treat it as a "what I'd add next" item.

Shall I go ahead with option 2 from before (the rules enforced inside `Trade`), plus the resulting-position preview in the ticket? Or do you want Sell Short as well?

```
using System.Text.RegularExpressions;

namespace TradeBlotter.Api.Domain;

public enum TradeSide
{
    Buy,
    Sell,
}

/// <summary>
/// An executed equity trade. Immutable, and valid by construction: an instance with a missing
/// symbol, a non-positive quantity or price, or no timestamp cannot exist.
/// </summary>
/// <remarks>
/// Quantity is always positive and direction comes only from <see cref="Side"/>, as in FIX.
/// "Buy -200" is not a short: going short is the position that results from selling more than is
/// held, so it is booked as "Sell 200". Allowing a sign as well would give two spellings of every
/// trade and let a stray minus sign book the opposite of the side the trader chose.
/// </remarks>
public sealed partial class Trade
{
    /// <summary>Upper-case ticker: a letter, then letters, digits, '.' or '-' (e.g. BRK.B), 12 at most.</summary>
    public const int MaxSymbolLength = 12;

    // EF Core also materializes stored trades through this constructor (parameters bind to the
    // properties by name), so rows read from the database are checked against the same rules.
    public Trade(string symbol, TradeSide side, int quantity, decimal price, DateTimeOffset timestamp)
    {
        var normalized = symbol?.Trim().ToUpperInvariant() ?? string.Empty;
        if (!SymbolFormat().IsMatch(normalized))
        {
            throw new ArgumentException(
                $"Symbol '{symbol}' is not a ticker: a letter, then letters, digits, '.' or '-', at most {MaxSymbolLength}.",
                nameof(symbol));
        }

        if (!Enum.IsDefined(side))
        {
            throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(side), side, "Side must be Buy or Sell.");
        }

        if (quantity <= 0)
        {
            throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(
                nameof(quantity), quantity, "Quantity must be a positive number of shares; direction comes from Side.");
        }

        if (price <= 0)
        {
            throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(price), price, "Price must be greater than 0.");
        }

        if (timestamp == default)
        {
            throw new ArgumentException("A trade needs the time it was booked.", nameof(timestamp));
        }

        Symbol = normalized;
        Side = side;
        Quantity = quantity;
        Price = price;
        Timestamp = timestamp.ToUniversalTime();
    }

    /// <summary>Assigned by the database when the trade is saved.</summary>
    public long Id { get; private set; }

    /// <summary>Ticker, upper case (e.g. AAPL).</summary>
    public string Symbol { get; }

    public TradeSide Side { get; }

    /// <summary>Number of shares; always positive. Direction comes from <see cref="Side"/>.</summary>
    public int Quantity { get; }

    /// <summary>Price per share; always positive.</summary>
    public decimal Price { get; }

    /// <summary>When the trade was booked, in UTC.</summary>
    public DateTimeOffset Timestamp { get; }

    /// <summary>Quantity signed by side: positive for Buy, negative for Sell.</summary>
    public long SignedQuantity => Side == TradeSide.Buy ? Quantity : -(long)Quantity;

    [GeneratedRegex(@"^[A-Z][A-Z0-9.\-]{0,11}$")]
    private static partial Regex SymbolFormat();
}

```

```
public static async Task<IReadOnlyList<Trade>> LoadAsync(string path, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    {
        await using var stream = File.OpenRead(path);
        var file = await JsonSerializer.DeserializeAsync<SeedFile>(stream, Json, cancellationToken)
            ?? throw new InvalidDataException($"{path} is empty.");

        return file.Trades
            .Select((t, i) =>
            {
                if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(t.Symbol) || t.Quantity <= 0 || t.Price <= 0)
                {
                    throw new InvalidDataException($"{path}: trade {i} needs a symbol and a positive quantity and price.");
                }

                return new Trade
                {
                    Symbol = t.Symbol.Trim().ToUpperInvariant(),
                    Side = t.Side,
                    Quantity = t.Quantity,
                    Price = t.Price,
                    Timestamp = t.Timestamp.ToUniversalTime(),
                };
            })
            .OrderBy(t => t.Timestamp)
            .ToList();
    }
```

```
namespace TradeBlotter.Api.Tests;

public class TradeTests
{
    private static readonly DateTimeOffset BookedAt = new(2026, 10, 23, 16, 0, 0, TimeSpan.FromHours(-4));

    [Fact]
    public void A_valid_trade_is_normalized()
    {
        var trade = new Trade(" brk.b ", TradeSide.Buy, 100, 542.19m, BookedAt);

        Assert.Equal("BRK.B", trade.Symbol);
        Assert.Equal(TimeSpan.Zero, trade.Timestamp.Offset);
        Assert.Equal(BookedAt, trade.Timestamp); // same instant, stored in UTC
    }

    [Theory]
    [InlineData(0)]
    [InlineData(-200)] // "Buy -200" is not a short; a short is booked as "Sell 200"
    public void Quantity_must_be_positive(int quantity)
    {
        var e = Assert.Throws<ArgumentOutOfRangeException>(
            () => new Trade("AAPL", TradeSide.Buy, quantity, 100m, BookedAt));

        Assert.Equal("quantity", e.ParamName);
    }

    [Theory]
    [InlineData("0")]
    [InlineData("-1.5")]
    public void Price_must_be_positive(string price)
    {
        var e = Assert.Throws<ArgumentOutOfRangeException>(
            () => new Trade("AAPL", TradeSide.Buy, 1, decimal.Parse(price), BookedAt));

        Assert.Equal("price", e.ParamName);
    }

    [Theory]
    [InlineData("")]
    [InlineData("   ")]
    [InlineData("1AAPL")]
    [InlineData("AA PL")]
    [InlineData("TOOLONGSYMBOL")]
    public void Symbol_must_be_a_ticker(string symbol)
    {
        var e = Assert.Throws<ArgumentException>(() => new Trade(symbol, TradeSide.Buy, 1, 1m, BookedAt));

        Assert.Equal("symbol", e.ParamName);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Side_must_be_Buy_or_Sell()
    {
        var e = Assert.Throws<ArgumentOutOfRangeException>(
            () => new Trade("AAPL", (TradeSide)7, 1, 1m, BookedAt));

        Assert.Equal("side", e.ParamName);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Timestamp_is_required()
    {
        var e = Assert.Throws<ArgumentException>(() => new Trade("AAPL", TradeSide.Buy, 1, 1m, default));

        Assert.Equal("timestamp", e.ParamName);
    }

    [Theory]
    [InlineData(TradeSide.Buy, 200)]
    [InlineData(TradeSide.Sell, -200)]
    public void Side_alone_sets_the_direction(TradeSide side, long signed)
    {
        Assert.Equal(signed, new Trade("AAPL", side, 200, 1m, BookedAt).SignedQuantity);
    }
}
```

```bash
## 16. Trade enforces its own invariants; quantity is never signed

**Decision:** `Trade` has one constructor that validates symbol format, side, quantity > 0, price > 0 and a timestamp,
and normalizes the symbol (upper case) and the timestamp (UTC). Its properties have private `init` accessors.
**Why:** Before this, only `Symbol` was `required`, and only to satisfy the compiler's nullable check. Nothing in the
type itself stopped a trade with quantity 0 or no timestamp. Now no layer (controller, seeder, tests, EF
materialization) can create an invalid `Trade`. The request DTO keeps its own validation for user-facing 400s.
**Direction:** "Buy −200" is rejected, not treated as a short. A short is a resulting position, and booking it as
"Sell 200" keeps one spelling per trade, so a stray minus sign can't flip the trader's chosen side. A "Sell Short"
side (as in FIX, for Reg SHO purposes) would be the way to flag short sales explicitly. It's not built.
**Trade-off:** The validation rules exist in the request (as attributes) and in the domain (in code). They match
today, and the domain is the one that cannot be bypassed.
"""
open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8',newline='\n').write(s)
```

**Claude:**

The earlier work is committed, and option 2 is built: a `Trade` can no longer be created with invalid values. All 39 API tests pass.

**Committed first,** as you asked:
```
090694b Document seed data, live prices and the Positions page
8d8b36c Add live Bloomberg prices, a Positions page, quick filters and a theme toggle
572ab07 Seed the dev database with a simulated peer-pairs book from IBKR closes
fca7fcf Initial commit
```

**Option 2:**
- **One constructor that checks everything.** `new Trade(symbol, side, quantity, price, timestamp)` rejects a malformed symbol, an unknown side, a quantity or price of zero or less (so "Buy −200" fails, with a message that direction comes from the side), and a missing timestamp. It upper-cases the symbol and converts the time to UTC.
- **Nothing can change a trade afterwards.** The properties can only be set inside the class.
- **One rule set everywhere.** The controller, the seed loader and the tests now all create trades through that constructor, and so does EF Core when it loads trades from the database. A bad seed file now names the line that broke the rules.
- **API behaviour is unchanged.** Bad requests still get a 400 with a message per field, as before.

**Tests:** 14 new `Trade` tests cover the rules, including "Buy −200 is rejected" and "the side alone sets the direction". With the earlier 25, that's 39.

**One fix along the way:** EF Core ignores properties that have no setter, so `Quantity` and `Price` were unmapped and every database test failed. Private `init` setters fixed it while keeping the type immutable. EF's model check confirms there's no schema change, so no migration is needed.

**You need to restart the API:** press **Ctrl+R** in your `dotnet watch` window. A constructor change is too big for hot reload, so your running API may still be on the old code.

Two changes, then:

1. **A year of seed trades.** I'll extend the generator from 3 month ends to 12 (October 2025 to September 2026) and pull two years of IBKR history, so the first rebalance has its 60-session lookback.
2. **Column filters.** The chip bars go away, replaced by a row of inputs under the column headers on both tables. Each input takes expressions:

| Type | Examples |
|---|---|
| Numbers | `>5`, `<=100`, `5\|6` (either), `>5&<10` (both), `10..20` (range), `!0` (not) |
| Text | `ko` (contains), `=KO` (exact), `ko\|pep`, `!t` (doesn't contain) |
| Dates (Time) | `2026-09` (that month), `>=2026-09-01` |

```
/**
 * Filter expressions typed under a column header.
 *
 *   |   either side matches (OR)          ko|pep        >100|<-100
 *   &   both sides match (AND), binds     >5&<10        !ko&!pep
 *       tighter than |                    >5&<10|=0  means  (>5 and <10) or =0
 *
 * Numbers: 5 (equals), >5 >=5 <5 <=5, =5, !5 or !=5 (not), 10..20 (inclusive range), !10..20.
 *          Commas are ignored, so 1,000 works; negatives work (<-100).
 * Text:    ko (contains, any case), =ko (exactly), !ko (does not contain), !=ko (is not).
 * Dates:   YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD. 2026-09 (that month), >=2026-09-01, 2026-01..2026-03.
 *          A shorter date compares at its own precision: >2026-09 means October onwards.
 *
 * An empty or null cell matches only an empty filter.
 */
export type FilterKind = 'text' | 'number' | 'date'

export type CompiledFilter =
  | { ok: true; test: (value: unknown) => boolean }
  | { ok: false; error: string }

type Predicate = (value: unknown) => boolean

const OPERATOR = /^(>=|<=|!=|>|<|=|!)?\s*(.*)$/
const DATE = /^\d{4}(-\d{2}(-\d{2})?)?$/

/** null when the expression is empty (no filtering); otherwise a test or an error to show. */
export function compileFilter(expression: string, kind: FilterKind): CompiledFilter | null {
  if (expression.trim() === '') return null
  try {
    const alternatives = expression.split('|').map((alternative) => {
      const conditions = alternative.split('&').map((c) => compileCondition(c.trim(), kind))
      return (value: unknown) => conditions.every((condition) => condition(value))
    })
    return {
      ok: true,
      test: (value) => value !== null && value !== undefined && value !== '' && alternatives.some((a) => a(value)),
    }
  } catch (e) {
    return { ok: false, error: e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e) }
  }
}

function compileCondition(text: string, kind: FilterKind): Predicate {
  if (text === '') throw new Error('Something is missing either side of | or &')
  const [, op = '', rawValue = ''] = OPERATOR.exec(text)!
  const value = rawValue.trim()
  if (value === '') throw new Error(`"${op}" needs a value after it`)

  switch (kind) {
    case 'number':
      return numberCondition(op, value)
    case 'date':
      return dateCondition(op, value)
    default:
      return textCondition(op, value)
  }
}

function parseNumber(text: string): number {
  const n = Number(text.replace(/[,\s]/g, ''))
  if (text === '' || !Number.isFinite(n)) throw new Error(`"${text}" is not a number`)
  return n
}

/** Split "a..b" into its ends; null when it is not a range. */
function splitRange(value: string): [string, string] | null {
  const parts = value.split('..')
  if (parts.length === 1) return null
  if (parts.length !== 2 || !parts[0]!.trim() || !parts[1]!.trim()) {
    throw new Error('A range is written low..high')
  }
  return [parts[0]!.trim(), parts[1]!.trim()]
}

function numberCondition(op: string, value: string): Predicate {
  const range = splitRange(value)
  if (range) {
    if (op && op !== '!' && op !== '!=') throw new Error('A range takes no operator other than !')
    const [lo, hi] = range.map(parseNumber) as [number, number]
    const inside = (v: unknown) => typeof v === 'number' && v >= Math.min(lo, hi) && v <= Math.max(lo, hi)
    return op ? (v) => typeof v === 'number' && !inside(v) : inside
  }

  const n = parseNumber(value)
  const num = (f: (v: number) => boolean): Predicate => (v) => typeof v === 'number' && f(v)
  switch (op) {
    case '>':
      return num((v) => v > n)
    case '>=':
      return num((v) => v >= n)
    case '<':
      return num((v) => v < n)
    case '<=':
      return num((v) => v <= n)
    case '!':
    case '!=':
      return num((v) => !sameNumber(v, n))
    default:
      return num((v) => sameNumber(v, n))
  }
}

/** Equal to the precision typed: 92.71 matches 92.71 but not 92.715. */
const sameNumber = (a: number, b: number) => Math.abs(a - b) < 1e-9
```

```
import { computed, reactive } from 'vue'
import { compileFilter, type FilterKind } from '@/utils/columnFilter'

export interface FilterColumn<T, K extends string> {
  key: K
  kind: FilterKind
  /** The value the filter tests: a number for number columns, YYYY-MM-DD for dates, text otherwise. */
  value: (row: T) => unknown
}

const PLACEHOLDERS: Record<FilterKind, string> = {
  number: '>5, 5|6, 10..20',
  text: 'ko|pep, !t',
  date: '2026-09, >=2026-09-01',
}

export const FILTER_HELP: Record<FilterKind, string> = {
  number: 'Numbers: 5, >5, >=5, <5, <=5, !5 (not), 10..20 (range). | for or, & for and: >5&<10|0',
  text: 'Text: ko (contains), =ko (exactly), !ko (not containing). | for or, & for and: ko|pep',
  date: 'Dates: 2026, 2026-09, 2026-09-30, >=2026-09-01, 2026-01..2026-03. | for or, & for and',
}

/**
 * One filter input per column, combined with AND across columns. Invalid expressions are
 * reported for that column and ignored, so a half-typed ">" never empties the table.
 */
export function useColumnFilters<T, K extends string>(
  rows: () => T[],
  columns: FilterColumn<T, K>[],
) {
  const filters = reactive(Object.fromEntries(columns.map((c) => [c.key, ''])) as Record<K, string>)

  const compiled = computed(() =>
    columns.map((column) => ({ column, filter: compileFilter(filters[column.key], column.kind) })),
  )

  const errors = computed(() => {
    const out = {} as Partial<Record<K, string>>
    for (const { column, filter } of compiled.value) {
      if (filter && !filter.ok) out[column.key] = filter.error
    }
    return out
  })

  const filtered = computed(() => {
    const active = compiled.value.flatMap(({ column, filter }) =>
      filter?.ok ? [{ value: column.value, test: filter.test }] : [],
    )
    if (active.length === 0) return rows()
    return rows().filter((row) => active.every(({ value, test }) => test(value(row))))
  })

  const isFiltered = computed(() => compiled.value.some(({ filter }) => filter?.ok))

  function clear() {
    for (const column of columns) filters[column.key] = ''
  }

  return { filters, errors, filtered, isFiltered, clear, placeholder: PLACEHOLDERS, help: FILTER_HELP }
}

```

```
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
import { compileFilter, type FilterKind } from '../columnFilter'

/** The values from `values` that `expression` keeps. */
function keep<T>(expression: string, kind: FilterKind, values: T[]): T[] {
  const filter = compileFilter(expression, kind)
  if (!filter) return values
  if (!filter.ok) throw new Error(filter.error)
  return values.filter((v) => filter.test(v))
}

function errorOf(expression: string, kind: FilterKind) {
  const filter = compileFilter(expression, kind)
  return filter && !filter.ok ? filter.error : null
}

describe('compileFilter: numbers', () => {
  const values = [-200, -5, 0, 5, 6, 10, 15, 20, 1000]

  it.each([
    ['5', [5]],
    ['=5', [5]],
    ['>5', [6, 10, 15, 20, 1000]],
    ['>=5', [5, 6, 10, 15, 20, 1000]],
    ['<0', [-200, -5]],
    ['<=-5', [-200, -5]],
    ['!5', [-200, -5, 0, 6, 10, 15, 20, 1000]],
    ['!=5', [-200, -5, 0, 6, 10, 15, 20, 1000]],
    ['5|6', [5, 6]],
    ['>5&<20', [6, 10, 15]],
    ['>5&<20|-200', [-200, 6, 10, 15]],
    ['10..20', [10, 15, 20]],
    ['20..10', [10, 15, 20]],
    ['!10..20', [-200, -5, 0, 5, 6, 1000]],
    ['-5..5', [-5, 0, 5]],
    ['1,000', [1000]],
    [' > 5 & < 20 ', [6, 10, 15]],
  ])('%s', (expression, expected) => {
    expect(keep(expression, 'number', values)).toEqual(expected)
  })

  it('matches decimals at the precision typed', () => {
    expect(keep('92.71', 'number', [92.71, 92.715, 92.7])).toEqual([92.71])
  })

  it('never matches a missing value', () => {
    expect(keep('!5', 'number', [null, 4])).toEqual([4])
  })

  it.each([
    ['>', '">" needs a value after it'],
    ['abc', '"abc" is not a number'],
    ['5|', 'Something is missing either side of | or &'],
    ['>1..2', 'A range takes no operator other than !'],
    ['1..', 'A range is written low..high'],
  ])('reports %s as invalid', (expression, error) => {
    expect(errorOf(expression, 'number')).toBe(error)
  })

  it('treats an empty expression as no filter', () => {
    expect(compileFilter('   ', 'number')).toBeNull()
  })
})

describe('compileFilter: text', () => {
  const values = ['KO', 'PEP', 'T', 'TMUS', 'TGT']

  it.each([
    ['t', ['T', 'TMUS', 'TGT']],
    ['=t', ['T']],
    ['!t', ['KO', 'PEP']],
    ['!=t', ['KO', 'PEP', 'TMUS', 'TGT']],
    ['ko|pep', ['KO', 'PEP']],
    ['t&!=t', ['TMUS', 'TGT']],
    ['KO', ['KO']],
  ])('%s', (expression, expected) => {
    expect(keep(expression, 'text', values)).toEqual(expected)
  })

  it('rejects comparisons on text', () => {
    expect(errorOf('>a', 'text')).toBe('Text filters take contains, = or !')
  })
})

describe('compileFilter: dates', () => {
  const values = ['2025-12-31', '2026-01-30', '2026-03-31', '2026-09-30', '2026-10-23']

  it.each([
    ['2026', ['2026-01-30', '2026-03-31', '2026-09-30', '2026-10-23']],
    ['2026-09', ['2026-09-30']],
    ['2026-09-30', ['2026-09-30']],
    ['>2026-09', ['2026-10-23']],
    ['>=2026-09-01', ['2026-09-30', '2026-10-23']],
    ['<2026', ['2025-12-31']],
    ['2026-01..2026-03', ['2026-01-30', '2026-03-31']],
    ['2025|2026-10', ['2025-12-31', '2026-10-23']],
    ['!2026', ['2025-12-31']],
  ])('%s', (expression, expected) => {
    expect(keep(expression, 'date', values)).toEqual(expected)
  })

  it('rejects something that is not a date', () => {
    expect(errorOf('sept', 'date')).toBe('"sept" is not a date (YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD)')
  })
})

```

**Claude:**

Both changes are done and work in a real browser. All 106 frontend tests and 39 API tests pass.

**A year of trades.** The seed now has **103 trades** at each month end from 31 Oct 2025 to 30 Sep 2026, all at real IBKR closes. One change to the book: FedEx is out. IBKR has adjusted FDX's prices from before the June 2026 FedEx Freight spin-off, so a year of FDX trades would have used prices that never actually traded, and the generator refused them. I swapped the Parcel group (UPS/FDX) for **Card networks (V/MA/AXP)**. There are still 6 groups, ending with 6 longs and 6 shorts.

**You won't see the year yet.** Your database still has the old 30 trades, and the seed only loads into an empty database. To reload it:
1. Stop `run_api.ps1` with Ctrl+C.
2. Delete `api\src\TradeBlotter.Api\trade-blotter.db*`.
3. Start it again.

That deletes the AAPL short you booked. I haven't touched your database.

**Column filters.** The chip buttons are gone. Each column now has an input under its header, filters in different columns combine with AND, and hovering an input shows its syntax:

| Column type | Examples |
|---|---|
| Numbers | `5`, `>5`, `<=-100`, `!0`, `10..20`, `5\|6`, `>5&<10`, `>5&<10\|0` (`&` binds tighter) |
| Text | `ko` (contains), `=ko` (exactly), `!t` (doesn't contain), `ko\|pep` |
| Dates (blotter Time) | `2026`, `2026-09`, `>=2026-09-01`, `2026-01..2026-03` |

- **Half-typed or invalid input:** something like `>` turns the input red, the tooltip says why, and the table stays unfiltered rather than going empty.
- **Positions totals follow the filters:** the screenshot shows `<0` on Net qty with `>0` on Unrealized P&L, leaving the 3 profitable shorts with totals for just those.
- **Text filters match "contains":** so `f|gm` also matches FDX. Use `=f|=gm` for exact symbols.
- **Header stays visible:** the blotter's header row and filter inputs stay at the top while you scroll.
- **Tests:** the filter syntax has 48 tests of its own.

Two batches of work are uncommitted: the `Trade` rules from before, and this one. Want me to commit them as two commits?

```
})
```

```
import type { ColDef, DoesFilterPassParams } from 'ag-grid-community'
import { compileFilter, type CompiledFilter, type FilterKind } from '@/utils/columnFilter'
import ExpressionFilterInput from './ExpressionFilterInput.vue'

/** filterParams for an expression-filtered column: the filter reads `value(row)`, not the cell text. */
export interface ExpressionFilterParams<T> {
  kind: FilterKind
  value: (row: T) => unknown
}

// The grid calls doesFilterPass for every row; compile each expression once.
const compiled = new Map<string, CompiledFilter | null>()
function compile(expression: string, kind: FilterKind) {
  const key = `${kind}\u0000${expression}`
  if (!compiled.has(key)) compiled.set(key, compileFilter(expression, kind))
  return compiled.get(key)!
}

/**
 * Column settings that give a column the expression filter (see utils/columnFilter.ts) as its
 * AG Grid filter, typed in the floating filter row under the header. The filter's model is the
 * expression string; the input only reports an expression to the grid once it is valid.
 */
export function expressionFilter<T>(kind: FilterKind, value: (row: T) => unknown): Partial<ColDef<T>> {
  return {
    filter: {
      component: ExpressionFilterInput,
      doesFilterPass: ({ model, node }: DoesFilterPassParams<T, unknown, string>) => {
        const filter = compile(model, kind)
        return !filter || !filter.ok || (node.data !== undefined && filter.test(value(node.data)))
      },
    },
    filterParams: { kind, value } satisfies ExpressionFilterParams<T>,
    floatingFilter: true,
    floatingFilterComponent: ExpressionFilterInput,
    suppressHeaderFilterButton: true,
  }
}
```

```
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, ref, watch } from 'vue'
import type { ColDef } from 'ag-grid-community'
import { compileFilter, FILTER_HELP, FILTER_PLACEHOLDER, type FilterKind } from '@/utils/columnFilter'

/**
 * The expression filter's input, used both as the floating filter under a header and as the
 * filter's own display. Both kinds of params carry the current model and onModelChange.
 */
const props = defineProps<{
  params: {
    model: string | null
    onModelChange: (model: string | null) => void
    colDef: ColDef
  }
}>()

const kind = computed<FilterKind>(() => (props.params.colDef.filterParams?.kind as FilterKind) ?? 'text')
const label = computed(() => `Filter ${props.params.colDef.headerName ?? ''}`.trim())

const text = ref(props.params.model ?? '')
const compiled = computed(() => compileFilter(text.value, kind.value))
const error = computed(() => (compiled.value && !compiled.value.ok ? compiled.value.error : null))

// Only valid expressions reach the grid; a half-typed ">" leaves the column unfiltered.
watch(compiled, (filter) => {
  const model = filter?.ok ? text.value.trim() : null
  if (model !== props.params.model) props.params.onModelChange(model)
})

// The grid changed the model (e.g. "Clear filters"): show it, unless the user is mid-way
// through an invalid expression that the grid never saw.
watch(
  () => props.params.model,
  (model) => {
    if (model === null && error.value) return
    if ((model ?? '') !== text.value.trim()) text.value = model ?? ''
  },
)
</script>

<template>
  <input
    v-model="text"
    class="expression-filter"
    :class="[kind, { invalid: error, active: text.trim() !== '' && !error }]"
    :placeholder="FILTER_PLACEHOLDER[kind]"
    :title="error ?? FILTER_HELP[kind]"
    :aria-label="label"
    :aria-invalid="!!error"
    spellcheck="false"
    autocomplete="off"
    @keydown.esc="text = ''"
  />
</template>

```

```
/* Shared AG Grid styling. Global, because the grid renders its own DOM outside component scopes. */

.grid {
  width: 100%;
  height: 100%;
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
}

/* Numbers: monospace, right-aligned, aligned digits. */
.grid .cell-num {
  justify-content: flex-end;
  text-align: right;
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
}

.grid .ag-header-cell.cell-num .ag-header-cell-label {
  flex-direction: row-reverse;
}

.grid .cell-symbol {
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  font-weight: 700;
}

.grid .cell-muted {
  color: var(--color-text-muted);
}

.grid .gain {
  color: var(--color-buy);
}

.grid .loss {
  color: var(--color-sell);
}

/* Buy/sell or long/short shown on the row's left edge, so runs read at a glance. */
.grid .ag-row.edge-buy,
.grid .ag-row.edge-sell {
  box-shadow: inset 2px 0 0 var(--row-edge);
}

.grid .ag-row.edge-buy {
  --row-edge: var(--color-buy);
}

.grid .ag-row.edge-sell {
  --row-edge: var(--color-sell);
}

.grid .side-badge {
  display: inline-block;
  min-width: 2.6rem;
  padding: 0 0.3rem;
  border-radius: 2px;
  font-size: 0.68rem;
  font-weight: 700;
  line-height: 1.35;
  letter-spacing: 0.04em;
  text-align: center;
  text-transform: uppercase;
}

.grid .side-badge.buy {
  background: var(--color-buy-bg);
  color: var(--color-buy);
}

.grid .side-badge.sell {
  background: var(--color-sell-bg);
  color: var(--color-sell);
}

.grid .direction {
  margin-left: 0.3rem;
  font-family: var(--font-sans);
  font-size: 0.62rem;
  font-weight: 700;
  letter-spacing: 0.04em;
}

/* Pinned totals row. */
.grid .ag-floating-bottom .ag-row {
  font-weight: 700;
  background: var(--color-surface-muted);
}

/* ---------- expression filter input (floating filter row) ---------- */
.expression-filter {
  width: 100%;
  height: 18px;
  padding: 0 0.3rem;
  border: 1px solid var(--color-border);
  border-radius: 2px;
  background: var(--color-surface);
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  font-size: 11px;
  color: var(--color-text);
}

.expression-filter.number {
  text-align: right;
}

.expression-filter::placeholder {
  color: var(--color-text-muted);
  opacity: 0.5;
}

.expression-filter.active {
  border-color: var(--color-accent);
}

.expression-filter.invalid {
  border-color: var(--color-danger);
  background: var(--color-sell-bg);
}

.expression-filter:focus {
  outline: none;
  border-color: var(--color-accent);
}
```

```
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, ref, shallowRef } from 'vue'
import { storeToRefs } from 'pinia'
import { AgGridVue } from 'ag-grid-vue3'
import type { ColDef, GridApi, GridReadyEvent, RowClassParams } from 'ag-grid-community'
import type { Trade } from '@/api/trades'
import { expressionFilter } from '@/grid/expressionFilter'
import { gridTheme } from '@/grid/theme'
import { useBlotterStore } from '@/stores/blotter'
import { formatAmount, formatPrice, formatQuantity, formatTimestamp } from '@/utils/format'

const blotter = useBlotterStore()
const { trades, newTradeIds, loading } = storeToRefs(blotter)

/** The trade's date as YYYY-MM-DD in the viewer's time zone, matching what the Time column shows. */
const localDate = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA', { year: 'numeric', month: '2-digit', day: '2-digit' })

const columnDefs: ColDef<Trade>[] = [
  {
    headerName: 'Time',
    field: 'timestamp',
    sort: 'desc',
    width: 128,
    cellClass: 'cell-num cell-muted',
    headerClass: 'cell-num',
    valueFormatter: (p) => (p.value ? formatTimestamp(p.value) : ''),
    tooltipValueGetter: (p) => (p.value ? new Date(p.value).toLocaleString() : ''),
    comparator: (a: string, b: string, nodeA, nodeB) =>
      Date.parse(a) - Date.parse(b) || (nodeA.data?.id ?? 0) - (nodeB.data?.id ?? 0),
    ...expressionFilter<Trade>('date', (t) => localDate.format(new Date(t.timestamp))),
  },
  {
    headerName: 'Symbol',
    field: 'symbol',
    width: 88,
    cellClass: 'cell-symbol',
    ...expressionFilter<Trade>('text', (t) => t.symbol),
  },
  {
    headerName: 'Side',
    field: 'side',
    width: 74,
    // Values are only ever Buy or Sell (validated by the API), so the markup is safe.
    cellRenderer: (p: { value: Trade['side'] }) =>
      `<span class="side-badge ${p.value === 'Buy' ? 'buy' : 'sell'}">${p.value === 'Buy' ? 'Buy' : 'Sell'}</span>`,
    ...expressionFilter<Trade>('text', (t) => t.side),
  },
  {
    headerName: 'Quantity',
    field: 'quantity',
    width: 96,
    cellClass: 'cell-num',
    headerClass: 'cell-num',
    valueFormatter: (p) => formatQuantity(p.value),
    ...expressionFilter<Trade>('number', (t) => t.quantity),
  },
  {
    headerName: 'Price',
    field: 'price',
    width: 96,
    cellClass: 'cell-num',
    headerClass: 'cell-num',
    valueFormatter: (p) => formatPrice(p.value),
    ...expressionFilter<Trade>('number', (t) => t.price),
  },
  {
    headerName: 'Notional',
    field: 'notional',
    minWidth: 110,
    flex: 1,
    cellClass: 'cell-num',
    headerClass: 'cell-num',
    valueFormatter: (p) => formatAmount(p.value),
    ...expressionFilter<Trade>('number', (t) => t.notional),
  },
]

const defaultColDef: ColDef<Trade> = { sortable: true, resizable: true, suppressMovable: false }

const api = shallowRef<GridApi<Trade>>()
const shown = ref(0)
const isFiltered = ref(false)

function onGridReady(event: GridReadyEvent<Trade>) {
  api.value = event.api
  refreshCount()
}

function refreshCount() {
  if (!api.value) return
  shown.value = api.value.getDisplayedRowCount()
  isFiltered.value = api.value.isAnyFilterPresent()
}

// Briefly highlight trades that arrived after the first load (own submissions and broadcasts).
const flashed = new Set<number>()
function onRowDataUpdated() {
  refreshCount()
  const nodes = [...newTradeIds.value]
    .filter((id) => !flashed.has(id))
    .map((id) => {
      flashed.add(id)
      return api.value?.getRowNode(String(id))
    })
    .filter((n) => n !== undefined)
  if (nodes.length) api.value?.flashCells({ rowNodes: nodes, flashDuration: 1500, fadeDuration: 1000 })
}

const countLabel = computed(() => {
  const total = `${trades.value.length} ${trades.value.length === 1 ? 'trade' : 'trades'}`
  return isFiltered.value ? `${shown.value} of ${total}` : total
})

const getRowId = (p: { data: Trade }) => String(p.data.id)
const rowClass = (p: RowClassParams<Trade>) => (p.data?.side === 'Buy' ? 'edge-buy' : 'edge-sell')
</script>
```

```
import type { IRowNode } from 'ag-grid-community'
import type { ValuedPosition } from '@/utils/valuePositions'

/**
 * A grid row on the Positions page. An expanded position is followed by a full-width "detail"
 * row carrying the same values, so filters and sorting treat the pair identically; postSortRows
 * then puts each detail row straight back under its position.
 */
export type PositionGridRow = ValuedPosition & { kind: 'position' | 'detail' }

export function toGridRows(positions: ValuedPosition[], expanded: ReadonlySet<string>): PositionGridRow[] {
  return positions.flatMap((p) =>
    expanded.has(p.symbol)
      ? [
          { ...p, kind: 'position' as const },
          { ...p, kind: 'detail' as const },
        ]
      : [{ ...p, kind: 'position' as const }],
  )
}

/** Re-attach each detail row directly below its position after the grid sorts. In place. */
export function keepDetailUnderParent(nodes: IRowNode<PositionGridRow>[]) {
  const details = new Map(
    nodes.filter((n) => n.data?.kind === 'detail').map((n) => [n.data!.symbol, n]),
  )
  if (details.size === 0) return
  const ordered: IRowNode<PositionGridRow>[] = []
  for (const node of nodes) {
    if (node.data?.kind === 'detail') continue
    ordered.push(node)
    const detail = node.data && details.get(node.data.symbol)
    if (detail) ordered.push(detail)
  }
  nodes.splice(0, nodes.length, ...ordered)
}
```

```
  else expanded.value.add(symbol)
}

function onRowClicked(event: RowClickedEvent<PositionGridRow>) {
```

```
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
import { flushPromises, mount, type VueWrapper } from '@vue/test-utils'
import { createPinia, setActivePinia } from 'pinia'
import type { Trade } from '@/api/trades'
import { useBlotterStore } from '@/stores/blotter'
import BlotterTable from '../BlotterTable.vue'

function trade(id: number, symbol: string, side: Trade['side'], minute: number): Trade {
  return {
    id,
    symbol,
    side,
    quantity: 10,
    price: 1,
    notional: 10,
    timestamp: new Date(Date.UTC(2026, 9, 24, 14, minute)).toISOString(),
  }
}

describe('BlotterTable (AG Grid)', () => {
  let wrapper: VueWrapper | undefined

  beforeEach(() => {
    setActivePinia(createPinia())
    useBlotterStore().trades = [
      trade(1, 'MSFT', 'Buy', 0),
      trade(2, 'AAPL', 'Sell', 5),
      trade(3, 'TSLA', 'Buy', 2),
    ]
  })

  afterEach(() => wrapper?.unmount())

  async function mountGrid() {
    wrapper = mount(BlotterTable, { attachTo: document.body })
    await flushPromises()
    return wrapper
  }

  /** Symbols of the displayed rows, top to bottom. */
  const symbols = (w: VueWrapper) =>
    w
      .findAll('.ag-row')
      .sort((a, b) => Number(a.attributes('row-index')) - Number(b.attributes('row-index')))
      .map((row) => row.find('[col-id="symbol"]').text())

  async function filter(w: VueWrapper, column: string, expression: string) {
    await w.find(`input[aria-label="Filter ${column}"]`).setValue(expression)
    await flushPromises()
  }

  it('shows newest trades first by default', async () => {
    const w = await mountGrid()

    expect(symbols(w)).toEqual(['AAPL', 'TSLA', 'MSFT'])
  })

  it('sorts by a column on header click, and reverses on a second click', async () => {
    const w = await mountGrid()
    const header = () => w.find('.ag-header-cell[col-id="symbol"] .ag-header-cell-label')

    await header().trigger('click')
    await flushPromises()
    expect(symbols(w)).toEqual(['AAPL', 'MSFT', 'TSLA'])

    await header().trigger('click')
    await flushPromises()
    expect(symbols(w)).toEqual(['TSLA', 'MSFT', 'AAPL'])
  })

  it('marks each row edge and badge with its side', async () => {
    const w = await mountGrid()
    const row = (index: number) => w.find(`.ag-row[row-index="${index}"]`)

    expect(row(0).classes()).toContain('edge-sell')
    expect(row(0).find('.side-badge').text()).toBe('Sell')
    expect(row(1).classes()).toContain('edge-buy')
  })

  it('filters with expressions typed under the headers, combined across columns', async () => {
    const w = await mountGrid()

    await filter(w, 'Side', '=buy')
    expect(symbols(w)).toEqual(['TSLA', 'MSFT'])
    expect(w.find('.count').text()).toContain('2 of 3 trades')

    await filter(w, 'Symbol', 'ms|aapl')
    expect(symbols(w)).toEqual(['MSFT'])

    await w.find('.filter-clear').trigger('click')
    await flushPromises()
    expect(symbols(w)).toEqual(['AAPL', 'TSLA', 'MSFT'])
    expect((w.find('input[aria-label="Filter Symbol"]').element as HTMLInputElement).value).toBe('')
  })

  it('takes number and date expressions', async () => {
    useBlotterStore().trades = [
      { ...trade(1, 'OLD', 'Buy', 0), quantity: 5, timestamp: '2025-12-15T15:00:00Z' },
      { ...trade(2, 'MID', 'Sell', 0), quantity: 6, timestamp: '2026-06-15T15:00:00Z' },
      { ...trade(3, 'NEW', 'Buy', 0), quantity: 500, timestamp: '2026-09-15T15:00:00Z' },
    ]
    const w = await mountGrid()

    await filter(w, 'Quantity', '5|6')
    expect(symbols(w)).toEqual(['MID', 'OLD'])

    await filter(w, 'Quantity', '>5')
    expect(symbols(w)).toEqual(['NEW', 'MID'])

    await filter(w, 'Quantity', '')
    await filter(w, 'Time', '<2026')
    expect(symbols(w)).toEqual(['OLD'])
  })

  it('marks an invalid expression and ignores it instead of emptying the grid', async () => {
    const w = await mountGrid()

    await filter(w, 'Price', '>')
    const input = w.find('input[aria-label="Filter Price"]')
```

```bash
p='src/grid/ExpressionFilterInput.vue'

s=s.replace("import { computed, ref, watch } from 'vue'","import { computed, ref, shallowRef, watch } from 'vue'")
old_start=s.index("const props = defineProps<{")
old_end=s.index("</script>")
s=s[:old_start]+"""type Params = {
  model: string | null
  onModelChange: (model: string | null) => void
  filterParams?: { kind?: FilterKind }
  colDef?: ColDef
  column?: Column
}

const props = defineProps<{ params: Params }>()

// The grid hands over new params (including the current model) through refresh(), not by
// re-rendering with new props, so keep the latest here.
const current = shallowRef<Params>(props.params)
function refresh(params: Params) {
  current.value = params
  return true
}
defineExpose({ refresh })

const colDef = computed(() => current.value.colDef ?? current.value.column?.getColDef())
const kind = computed<FilterKind>(
  () => current.value.filterParams?.kind ?? colDef.value?.filterParams?.kind ?? 'text',
)
const label = computed(() => `Filter ${colDef.value?.headerName ?? ''}`.trim())

const text = ref(current.value.model ?? '')
const compiled = computed(() => compileFilter(text.value, kind.value))
const error = computed(() => (compiled.value && !compiled.value.ok ? compiled.value.error : null))

// Only valid expressions reach the grid; a half-typed ">" leaves the column unfiltered.
watch(compiled, (filter) => {
  const model = filter?.ok ? text.value.trim() : null
  if (model !== current.value.model) current.value.onModelChange(model)
})

// The grid changed the model (e.g. "Clear filters"): show it, unless the user is mid-way
// through an invalid expression that the grid never saw.
watch(
  () => current.value.model,
  (model) => {
    if (model === null && error.value) return
    if ((model ?? '') !== text.value.trim()) text.value = model ?? ''
  },
)
"""+s[old_end:]
```

```
<script setup lang="ts">
import { onBeforeUnmount, onMounted, useTemplateRef } from 'vue'
import type { GridApi, IRowNode } from 'ag-grid-community'
import PositionDetail from '@/components/PositionDetail.vue'
import type { PositionGridRow } from './positionRows'

export interface DetailRowContext {
  /** Remember a detail row's measured height, so getRowHeight keeps it across data refreshes. */
  rememberDetailHeight(symbol: string, height: number): void
}

/** Full-width grid row under an expanded position: its description and price history. */
const props = defineProps<{
  params: {
    data: PositionGridRow
    node: IRowNode<PositionGridRow>
    api: GridApi<PositionGridRow>
    context: DetailRowContext
  }
}>()

// The panel's height depends on what Bloomberg returns, so size the row to its content
// instead of a fixed guess (which left a gap under the panel).
const content = useTemplateRef<HTMLDivElement>('content')
let observer: ResizeObserver | undefined

onMounted(() => {
  if (!content.value || typeof ResizeObserver === 'undefined') return
  observer = new ResizeObserver(() => {
    if (!content.value) return
    const height = Math.ceil(content.value.getBoundingClientRect().height) + 1 // + bottom rule
    props.params.context.rememberDetailHeight(props.params.data.symbol, height)
    if (props.params.node.rowHeight !== height) {
      props.params.node.setRowHeight(height)
      props.params.api.onRowHeightChanged()
    }
  })
  observer.observe(content.value)
})

onBeforeUnmount(() => observer?.disconnect())
</script>

<template>
  <div class="detail-row">
    <div ref="content">
      <PositionDetail
        :symbol="params.data.symbol"
        :average-cost="params.data.averageCost"
        :last="params.data.last"
      />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

.detail-row {

  box-shadow: inset 2px 0 0 var(--color-accent);
}
```

```bash
Enforce Trade invariants in the domain type

Trade now has a single validating constructor and immutable properties:
a ticker-shaped symbol (normalized to upper case), Buy or Sell, a
positive quantity and price, and a timestamp (stored in UTC). Before,
only Symbol was `required`, and only to satisfy nullable analysis, so
`new Trade { Symbol = "AAPL" }` compiled with zero quantity and price.

Quantity is never signed: "Buy -200" is rejected rather than read as a
short. A short is the position that results from selling, booked as
"Sell 200", so each trade has one spelling.

The controller, seeder and tests construct trades through it, and EF
Core materializes stored rows through the same constructor (private
init accessors keep the properties mapped). No schema change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <[email redacted]>
EOF

103 trades over the 12 month ends from October 2025 to September 2026,

generator refuses to fill at prices that never printed.
```

```bash
/**
 * Whether DeskLink is reachable and its Bloomberg session is open. Costs no Bloomberg data,
 * so it can be polled to show availability before any price is asked for.
 */
export async function fetchBloombergAvailable(signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<boolean> {
  try {
    const response = await fetch(`${DESKLINK_URL}/con/bloomberg/status`, { signal })
    const body = (await response.json()) as {
      ok?: boolean
      data?: { connected?: boolean; sessionReady?: boolean; switchedOff?: boolean }
    }
    return Boolean(body.ok && body.data?.connected && body.data.sessionReady && !body.data.switchedOff)
  } catch {
    return false
  }
}
EOF
cat > src/composables/useBloombergStatus.ts <<'EOF'
import { onScopeDispose, ref } from 'vue'
import { fetchBloombergAvailable } from '@/api/bloomberg'

/** Polls whether live Bloomberg prices are available on this desk (via DeskLink). */
export function useBloombergStatus(intervalMs = 30_000) {
  const available = ref<boolean | null>(null) // null until the first check answers

  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined
  const controller = new AbortController()

  async function check() {
    available.value = await fetchBloombergAvailable(controller.signal)
    if (!controller.signal.aborted) timer = setTimeout(check, intervalMs)
  }
  void check()

  onScopeDispose(() => {
    controller.abort()
    clearTimeout(timer)
  })

  return { available }
}
EOF
```

```
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
import type { IRowNode } from 'ag-grid-community'
import type { ValuedPosition } from '@/utils/valuePositions'
import { keepDetailUnderParent, toGridRows, type PositionGridRow } from '../positionRows'

const position = (symbol: string): ValuedPosition => ({
  symbol,
  name: null,
  netQuantity: 1,
  averageCost: 1,
  costBasis: 1,
  last: null,
  dayChangePercent: null,
  marketValue: null,
  unrealizedPnl: null,
  unrealizedPercent: null,
  dayPnl: null,
})

const node = (row: PositionGridRow) => ({ data: row }) as IRowNode<PositionGridRow>
const describeNodes = (nodes: IRowNode<PositionGridRow>[]) =>
  nodes.map((n) => `${n.data!.kind}:${n.data!.symbol}`)

describe('positionRows', () => {
  it('adds a detail row after each expanded position only', () => {
    const rows = toGridRows([position('KO'), position('PEP')], new Set(['KO']))

    expect(rows.map((r) => `${r.kind}:${r.symbol}`)).toEqual([
      'position:KO',
      'detail:KO',
      'position:PEP',
    ])
  })

  it('puts each detail row straight back under its position after a sort', () => {
    // As a sort could leave them: details separated from, or ahead of, their positions.
    const nodes = [
      { kind: 'detail', symbol: 'PEP' },
      { kind: 'position', symbol: 'WMT' },
      { kind: 'position', symbol: 'KO' },
      { kind: 'position', symbol: 'PEP' },
      { kind: 'detail', symbol: 'KO' },
    ].map((r) => node({ ...position(r.symbol), kind: r.kind as PositionGridRow['kind'] }))

    keepDetailUnderParent(nodes)

    expect(describeNodes(nodes)).toEqual([
      'position:WMT',
      'position:KO',
      'detail:KO',
      'position:PEP',
      'detail:PEP',
    ])
  })
})

```

```
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest'
import { flushPromises, mount, type VueWrapper } from '@vue/test-utils'
import { createPinia, setActivePinia } from 'pinia'
import type { LiveQuote, PricePoint, SecurityProfile } from '@/api/bloomberg'
import { useBlotterStore } from '@/stores/blotter'
import PositionsView from '../PositionsView.vue'

const bloomberg = vi.hoisted(() => ({
  fetchLiveQuotes: vi.fn<(symbols: string[]) => Promise<Map<string, LiveQuote>>>(),
  fetchSecurityProfile: vi.fn<(symbol: string) => Promise<SecurityProfile | null>>(),
  fetchPriceHistory: vi.fn<(symbol: string) => Promise<PricePoint[]>>(),
}))
vi.mock('@/api/bloomberg', () => bloomberg)

const quote = (symbol: string, last: number): LiveQuote => ({
  symbol,
  name: `${symbol} CORP`,
  last,
  changePercent: null,
  asOf: '2026-10-24T13:35:16Z',
})

describe('PositionsView (AG Grid)', () => {
  let wrapper: VueWrapper | undefined

  beforeEach(() => {
    setActivePinia(createPinia())
    useBlotterStore().positions = [
      { symbol: 'KO', netQuantity: -100, averageCost: 90 }, // short, price fell: gainer
      { symbol: 'PEP', netQuantity: 100, averageCost: 140 }, // long, price fell: loser
      { symbol: 'WMT', netQuantity: 50, averageCost: 100 }, // long, price rose: gainer
    ]
    bloomberg.fetchLiveQuotes.mockResolvedValue(
      new Map([
        ['KO', quote('KO', 85)],
        ['PEP', quote('PEP', 130)],
        ['WMT', quote('WMT', 110)],
      ]),
    )
    bloomberg.fetchSecurityProfile.mockResolvedValue(null)
    bloomberg.fetchPriceHistory.mockResolvedValue([])
  })

  afterEach(() => wrapper?.unmount())

  async function mountGrid() {
    wrapper = mount(PositionsView, { attachTo: document.body })
    await flushPromises()
    return wrapper
  }

  /** Symbols of the displayed position rows (not detail or totals rows), top to bottom. */
  const symbols = (w: VueWrapper) =>
    w
      .findAll('.ag-center-cols-container .ag-row, .ag-center-cols-viewport .ag-row')
      .filter((row) => !row.classes().includes('ag-full-width-row'))
      .sort((a, b) => Number(a.attributes('row-index')) - Number(b.attributes('row-index')))
      .map((row) => row.find('[col-id="symbol"]').text())
      .filter((s) => s && !s.startsWith('Total'))

  async function filter(w: VueWrapper, column: string, expression: string) {
    await w.find(`input[aria-label="Filter ${column}"]`).setValue(expression)
    await flushPromises()
  }

  it('lists positions marked to the live price, with a totals row', async () => {
    const w = await mountGrid()

    expect(symbols(w)).toEqual(['KO', 'PEP', 'WMT'])
    // Unrealized: KO +500, PEP −1,000, WMT +500
    expect(w.find('.ag-floating-bottom').text()).toContain('0.00')
  })

  it('filters with expressions, and the totals and summary follow the filter', async () => {
    const w = await mountGrid()

    await filter(w, 'Net qty', '>0')
    expect(symbols(w)).toEqual(['PEP', 'WMT'])

    await filter(w, 'Unrl P&L', '>0')
    expect(symbols(w)).toEqual(['WMT'])
    expect(w.find('.filter-count').text()).toContain('Showing 1 of 3')
    expect(w.find('.ag-floating-bottom').text()).toContain('+500.00') // WMT: (110 − 100) × 50
    expect(w.find('.summary').text()).toContain('+500.00')

    await w.find('.filter-clear').trigger('click')
    await flushPromises()
    expect(symbols(w)).toEqual(['KO', 'PEP', 'WMT'])
  })

  it('filters text columns with or', async () => {
    const w = await mountGrid()

    await filter(w, 'Name', 'pep corp|wmt')
    expect(symbols(w)).toEqual(['PEP', 'WMT'])
  })

  it('expands a row into a full-width detail row and collapses it again', async () => {
```

```
import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest'
import { flushPromises, mount } from '@vue/test-utils'
import { createPinia, setActivePinia } from 'pinia'
import type { Trade } from '@/api/trades'
import { useBlotterStore } from '@/stores/blotter'
import PositionDetail from '../PositionDetail.vue'

vi.mock('@/api/bloomberg', () => ({
  fetchSecurityProfile: async () => null,
  fetchPriceHistory: async () => [],
}))

const trade = (id: number, symbol: string, side: Trade['side'], quantity: number, day: number): Trade => ({
  id,
  symbol,
  side,
  quantity,
  price: 10 + id,
  notional: quantity * (10 + id),
  timestamp: new Date(Date.UTC(2026, 8, day, 20)).toISOString(),
})

describe('PositionDetail trade history', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    setActivePinia(createPinia())
    useBlotterStore().trades = [
      trade(1, 'KO', 'Buy', 100, 1),
      trade(2, 'PEP', 'Buy', 999, 2), // another symbol: not shown
      trade(3, 'KO', 'Sell', 100, 3), // flat
      trade(4, 'KO', 'Sell', 50, 4), // short 50
    ]
  })

  it('lists this symbol’s trades newest first with the position each one left', async () => {
    const wrapper = mount(PositionDetail, { props: { symbol: 'KO', averageCost: 14, last: 15 } })
    await flushPromises()

    const rows = wrapper.findAll('.trades tbody tr').map((tr) =>
      tr.findAll('td').map((td) => td.text()),
    )

    expect(wrapper.find('.trades .panel-title').text()).toContain('3')
    expect(rows.map((r) => [r[1], r[2], r[4]])).toEqual([
      ['Sell', '50', '-50'],
      ['Sell', '100', 'flat'],
      ['Buy', '100', '100'],
    ])
  })
})

```

```bash
 ("""Both tables have a **filter row under the column headers**:""","""The blotter and Positions tables are **AG Grid Community** grids with spreadsheet-height rows. Columns sort, resize and

│   ├── BlotterTable.vue               # sorting is local view state""","""├── grid/                              # AG Grid setup shared by both grids
│   ├── theme.ts                       # dense theme driven by the app's CSS colour tokens
│   ├── expressionFilter.ts            # the expression syntax as an AG Grid column filter
│   ├── ExpressionFilterInput.vue      # the input under each header
│   ├── positionRows.ts                # expanded positions -> full-width detail rows
│   └── PositionDetailRow.vue          # detail row; sizes itself to its content

│   ├── BlotterTable.vue               # AG Grid"""),

s=open('docs/decisions.md',encoding='utf-8').read().rstrip()+"""

## 17. AG Grid Community for the blotter and positions

**Decision:** Both tables are AG Grid Community (MIT) grids rather than hand-built HTML tables. The dense theme
is driven by the app's CSS tokens, rows are 24px, and the filter row under the headers is our expression syntax
plugged in as an AG Grid filter.
**Why:** The author asked for AG Grid behaviour and a sleek, efficient screen. Using AG Grid gives column
resize/move, virtualised scrolling for large histories, cell flashing on live prices and pinned totals, without
reimplementing them.
**Details:** Expanded positions are full-width rows, and `postSortRows` keeps each one under its position. Detail
rows measure their content, so there is no fixed-height gap. The filter input exposes `refresh()`, because the grid
passes the current model through it; without that, "Clear filters" left stale text (caught by a test).
**Trade-off:** About 1 MB more JavaScript, as `AllCommunityModule` is registered; registering only the modules used
```
