```bash
# 1. Trade invariants (API only)
git add api/src/TradeBlotter.Api/Domain/Trade.cs api/src/TradeBlotter.Api/Controllers/TradesController.cs api/src/TradeBlotter.Api/Data/TradeSeeder.cs api/tests/TradeBlotter.Api.Tests/PositionCalculatorTests.cs api/tests/TradeBlotter.Api.Tests/TradeTests.cs
git diff --cached --name-only
commit "Enforce Trade invariants in the domain type

Trade now has a single validating constructor and immutable properties:
a ticker-shaped symbol (normalized to upper case), Buy or Sell, a
positive quantity and price, and a timestamp (stored in UTC). Before,
only Symbol was \`required\`, and only to satisfy nullable analysis, so
\`new Trade { Symbol = \"AAPL\" }\` compiled with zero quantity and price.

Quantity is never signed: \"Buy -200\" is rejected rather than read as a
short. A short is the position that results from selling, booked as
\"Sell 200\", so each trade has one spelling.

The controller, seeder and tests construct trades through it, and EF
Core materializes stored rows through the same constructor (private
init accessors keep the properties mapped). No schema change."

# 2. Year of seed trades
git add tools/seed-peer-pairs/generate.mjs api/src/TradeBlotter.Api/Data/Seed/peer-pairs-trades.json docs/seed-portfolio.md
git diff --cached --name-only
commit "Extend the seed portfolio to a year of trades

103 trades over the 12 month ends from October 2025 to September 2026,
from two years of IBKR daily bars (for the 60-session lookback).

The Parcel group (UPS/FDX) is replaced by Card networks (V/MA/AXP):
IBKR back-adjusts FDX for the June 2026 FedEx Freight spin-off, and the
generator refuses to fill at prices that never printed."

# 3. Column filter expression syntax
git add app/src/utils/columnFilter.ts app/src/utils/__tests__/columnFilter.spec.ts
git diff --cached --name-only
commit "Add an expression syntax for column filters

A small language for filtering a column by typing under its header:
| (or), & (and, binds tighter), comparisons (> >= < <= = !), ranges
(10..20), text contains/exact/not, and dates compared at the precision
typed (2026-09 is the whole month). Invalid input is reported, never
applied, so a half-typed \">\" cannot empty a table. 48 tests."
git status --short | head -3
```

```bash
// ---------- technicals ----------

/** Bloomberg's own technical studies for a security on one day (or now). */
export interface Technicals {
  rsi14: number | null
  ma50: number | null
  ma200: number | null
  /** 30-day historical volatility, annualised, in percent. */
  vol30: number | null
}

const TECHNICAL_FIELDS = ['RSI_14D', 'MOV_AVG_50D', 'MOV_AVG_200D', 'VOLATILITY_30D'] as const

/** Technicals change slowly; let DeskLink's cache serve them for 15 minutes. */
const TECHNICALS_CACHE_SECONDS = 900

function toTechnicals(fields: Record<string, string | null | undefined> | undefined): Technicals {
  const n = (field: string) => {
    const raw = fields?.[field]
    const value = Number(raw)
    return raw === null || raw === undefined || raw === '' || !Number.isFinite(value) ? null : value
  }
  return { rsi14: n('RSI_14D'), ma50: n('MOV_AVG_50D'), ma200: n('MOV_AVG_200D'), vol30: n('VOLATILITY_30D') }
}

/** Current technicals for several symbols in one request, keyed by upper-case symbol. */
export async function fetchCurrentTechnicals(
  symbols: string[],
  signal?: AbortSignal,
): Promise<Map<string, Technicals>> {
  const unique = [...new Set(symbols.map(normalize))].filter(Boolean)
  const result = new Map<string, Technicals>()
  if (unique.length === 0) return result
  const data = await postDeskLink<NonNullable<BdpEnvelope['data']>>(
    '/con/bloomberg/bdp',
    {
      securities: unique.map(toBloombergSecurity),
      fields: [...TECHNICAL_FIELDS],
      mode: 'auto',
      ttlSeconds: TECHNICALS_CACHE_SECONDS,
    },
    signal,
  )
  for (const symbol of unique) {
    const fields = data.data?.[toBloombergSecurity(symbol)]
    if (fields) result.set(symbol, toTechnicals(fields))
  }
  return result
}

export interface DatedTechnicals extends Technicals {
  /** YYYY-MM-DD */
  date: string
}

/**
 * Daily technicals for several symbols between two dates, in one bdh request, keyed by
 * upper-case symbol, each list in date order.
 */
export async function fetchTechnicalsHistory(
  symbols: string[],
  startDate: string,
  endDate: string,
  signal?: AbortSignal,
): Promise<Map<string, DatedTechnicals[]>> {
  const unique = [...new Set(symbols.map(normalize))].filter(Boolean)
  const result = new Map<string, DatedTechnicals[]>()
  if (unique.length === 0) return result
  const data = await postDeskLink<Record<string, Record<string, string | null>[]>>(
    '/con/bloomberg/bdh',
    {
      securities: unique.map(toBloombergSecurity),
      fields: [...TECHNICAL_FIELDS],
      startDate,
      endDate,
      periodicitySelection: 'DAILY',
    },
    signal,
  )
  for (const symbol of unique) {
    const rows = data[toBloombergSecurity(symbol)] ?? []
    result.set(
      symbol,
      rows
        .map((row) => ({ date: String(row.date), ...toTechnicals(row) }))
        .sort((a, b) => a.date.localeCompare(b.date)),
    )
  }
  return result
}
```

```
import type { DatedTechnicals, Technicals } from '@/api/bloomberg'

/** What the grids show: RSI, price against the moving averages, and volatility. */
export interface TechnicalColumns {
  rsi14: number | null
  /** Price against the 50-day moving average, in percent (+5 = 5% above). */
  vsMa50: number | null
  vsMa200: number | null
  vol30: number | null
}

export const NO_TECHNICALS: TechnicalColumns = { rsi14: null, vsMa50: null, vsMa200: null, vol30: null }

const versus = (price: number | null, average: number | null) =>
  price !== null && average !== null && average > 0 ? (price / average - 1) * 100 : null

/** Display figures for a price (a trade's, or the live last) against Bloomberg's technicals. */
export function technicalColumns(price: number | null, t: Technicals | undefined): TechnicalColumns {
  if (!t) return NO_TECHNICALS
  return { rsi14: t.rsi14, vsMa50: versus(price, t.ma50), vsMa200: versus(price, t.ma200), vol30: t.vol30 }
}

/**
 * The technicals in effect on a date: that day's, or the last trading day before it (a trade
 * booked today, before Bloomberg has today's figures, uses yesterday's). `history` is in date order.
 */
export function technicalsOnDate(history: DatedTechnicals[], date: string): DatedTechnicals | undefined {
  let lo = 0
  let hi = history.length - 1
  let found: DatedTechnicals | undefined
  while (lo <= hi) {
    const mid = (lo + hi) >> 1
    if (history[mid]!.date <= date) {
      found = history[mid]
      lo = mid + 1
    } else {
      hi = mid - 1
    }
  }
  return found
}
```

```
import { computed, onScopeDispose, ref, shallowRef, watch } from 'vue'
import {
  fetchCurrentTechnicals,
  fetchTechnicalsHistory,
  type DatedTechnicals,
  type Technicals,
} from '@/api/bloomberg'
import type { Trade } from '@/api/trades'
import { technicalColumns, technicalsOnDate, type TechnicalColumns } from '@/utils/technicals'

export type TechnicalsStatus = 'idle' | 'loading' | 'ready' | 'unavailable'

/** The New York session a trade belongs to, as YYYY-MM-DD. */
const sessionDate = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA', { timeZone: 'America/New_York' })
const today = () => sessionDate.format(new Date())

/**
 * Bloomberg technicals as they stood when each trade was booked, keyed by trade id.
 * One bdh request covers every symbol not yet loaded, from the earliest trade to today.
 */
export function useTradeTechnicals(trades: () => Trade[]) {
  const histories = shallowRef<ReadonlyMap<string, DatedTechnicals[]>>(new Map())
  const status = ref<TechnicalsStatus>('idle')
  const requested = new Set<string>()
  const controller = new AbortController()
  onScopeDispose(() => controller.abort())

  async function load(symbols: string[], from: string) {
    symbols.forEach((s) => requested.add(s))
    status.value = 'loading'
    try {
      const loaded = await fetchTechnicalsHistory(symbols, from, today(), controller.signal)
      histories.value = new Map([...histories.value, ...loaded])
      status.value = 'ready'
    } catch {
      if (controller.signal.aborted) return
      symbols.forEach((s) => requested.delete(s)) // retried when the trades next change
      status.value = 'unavailable'
    }
  }

  watch(
    trades,
    (list) => {
      const missing = [...new Set(list.map((t) => t.symbol))].filter((s) => !requested.has(s))
      if (missing.length === 0) return
      const earliest = list.reduce(
        (min, t) => (t.timestamp < min ? t.timestamp : min),
        list[0]!.timestamp,
      )
      void load(missing, sessionDate.format(new Date(earliest)))
    },
    { immediate: true },
  )

  const byTrade = computed(() => {
    const map = new Map<number, TechnicalColumns>()
    for (const t of trades()) {
      const history = histories.value.get(t.symbol)
      if (!history) continue
      map.set(t.id, technicalColumns(t.price, technicalsOnDate(history, sessionDate.format(new Date(t.timestamp)))))
    }
    return map
  })

  return { byTrade, status }
}

/** Current Bloomberg technicals for a changing set of symbols, refreshed every few minutes. */
export function useCurrentTechnicals(symbols: () => string[], refreshMs = 5 * 60_000) {
  const technicals = shallowRef<ReadonlyMap<string, Technicals>>(new Map())
  const status = ref<TechnicalsStatus>('idle')
  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined
  let inFlight: AbortController | undefined

  async function load(list: string[]) {
    clearTimeout(timer)
    inFlight?.abort()
    const request = new AbortController()
    inFlight = request
    try {
      technicals.value = await fetchCurrentTechnicals(list, request.signal)
      status.value = 'ready'
    } catch {
      if (request.signal.aborted) return
      status.value = 'unavailable'
    }
    if (inFlight === request) timer = setTimeout(() => load(list), refreshMs)
  }

  watch(
    () => [...new Set(symbols())].sort().join(','),
    (key) => {
      if (!key) return
      if (status.value === 'idle') status.value = 'loading'
      void load(key.split(','))
    },
    { immediate: true },
  )

  onScopeDispose(() => {
    clearTimeout(timer)
    inFlight?.abort()
  })

  return { technicals, status }
}
```

```
import type { ColDef, ColGroupDef, ValueFormatterParams } from 'ag-grid-community'
import type { TechnicalColumns } from '@/utils/technicals'
import { expressionFilter } from './expressionFilter'

const signed1 = (v: number) => `${v > 0 ? '+' : v < 0 ? '−' : ''}${Math.abs(v).toFixed(1)}%`

/** "—" when there is no figure, blank in a pinned totals row. */
const show =
  (format: (v: number) => string) =>
  (p: ValueFormatterParams): string =>
    p.value === null || p.value === undefined ? (p.node?.rowPinned ? '' : '—') : format(p.value)

const signClasses = {
  gain: (p: { value: number | null }) => (p.value ?? 0) > 0,
  loss: (p: { value: number | null }) => (p.value ?? 0) < 0,
}

/**
 * Bloomberg's RSI(14), price against the 50- and 200-day averages, and 30-day volatility, as a
 * column group. Rows carry the figures as fields (see utils/technicals.ts).
 */
export function technicalColumnGroup<T extends TechnicalColumns>(
  headerName: string,
  headerTooltip: string,
): ColGroupDef<T> {
  const column = (
    field: keyof TechnicalColumns,
    header: string,
    width: number,
    tooltip: string,
    extra: Partial<ColDef<T>>,
  ) =>
    ({
      field,
      headerName: header,
      headerTooltip: tooltip,
      width,
      cellClass: 'cell-num',
      headerClass: 'cell-num',
      ...expressionFilter<T>('number', (row) => row[field]),
      ...extra,
    }) as ColDef<T>

  return {
    headerName,
    headerTooltip,
    headerClass: 'group-technicals',
    children: [
      column('rsi14', 'RSI', 56, 'RSI, 14-day. 70 and above is overbought, 30 and below oversold.', {
        valueFormatter: show((v) => v.toFixed(1)),
        cellClassRules: {
          'rsi-high': (p) => (p.value ?? 0) >= 70,
          'rsi-low': (p) => p.value !== null && p.value !== undefined && p.value <= 30,
        },
      }),
      column('vsMa50', 'vs 50D', 66, 'Price against the 50-day moving average', {
        valueFormatter: show(signed1),
        cellClassRules: signClasses,
      }),
      column('vsMa200', 'vs 200D', 70, 'Price against the 200-day moving average', {
        valueFormatter: show(signed1),
        cellClassRules: signClasses,
      }),
      column('vol30', 'Vol 30D', 66, '30-day historical volatility, annualised', {
        valueFormatter: show((v) => `${v.toFixed(1)}%`),
      }),
    ],
  }
}
```

```
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
import type { DatedTechnicals } from '@/api/bloomberg'
import { NO_TECHNICALS, technicalColumns, technicalsOnDate } from '../technicals'

const day = (date: string, rsi14: number): DatedTechnicals => ({
  date,
  rsi14,
  ma50: 100,
  ma200: 80,
  vol30: 25,
})

describe('technicals', () => {
  const history = [day('2026-09-28', 40), day('2026-09-29', 39), day('2026-09-30', 34)]

  it('uses the trade date’s figures when Bloomberg has them', () => {
    expect(technicalsOnDate(history, '2026-09-29')?.rsi14).toBe(39)
  })

  it('falls back to the last trading day before the trade (weekend, or today before the close)', () => {
    expect(technicalsOnDate(history, '2026-10-03')?.date).toBe('2026-09-30')
  })

  it('has nothing for a date before the history starts', () => {
    expect(technicalsOnDate(history, '2026-09-01')).toBeUndefined()
  })

  it('measures the price against the moving averages in percent', () => {
    expect(technicalColumns(110, { rsi14: 55, ma50: 100, ma200: 80, vol30: 25 })).toEqual({
      rsi14: 55,
      vsMa50: expect.closeTo(10, 9),
      vsMa200: expect.closeTo(37.5, 9),
      vol30: 25,
    })
  })

  it('leaves comparisons empty without a price or an average', () => {
    expect(technicalColumns(null, { rsi14: 55, ma50: 100, ma200: null, vol30: 25 })).toEqual({
      rsi14: 55,
      vsMa50: null,
      vsMa200: null,
      vol30: 25,
    })
    expect(technicalColumns(110, undefined)).toEqual(NO_TECHNICALS)
  })
})
```

```bash
## 18. Bloomberg technicals beside trades and positions

volatility on each trade's date. Positions shows the same figures, current.

- Fetched in the browser, like the prices (decision 15).

**Trade-off:** The blotter's request grows with history: about a year of daily bars for each traded symbol.
```

**Claude:**

I went with your first option: compact columns, then Bloomberg technicals in the space that was empty. Both grids now have a technicals column group, and it's committed.

- **Blotter ("At trade · Bloomberg"):** RSI(14), the trade price against the 50-day and 200-day moving averages, and 30-day volatility, all as they stood on the trade date. For example, the 30 Sep F buy came at RSI 28.7, which is oversold. It's one Bloomberg history request for all symbols, made once per session. A trade booked today uses yesterday's close, because Bloomberg doesn't have today's figures until the end of the day.
- **Positions ("Technicals · Bloomberg"):** the same four figures, current, with the averages compared with the live price. They refresh every 5 minutes.
- **Colours:** RSI turns red at 70 or above (overbought) and green at 30 or below (oversold). The average columns are green above and red below.
- **Filters:** they work like any number column, so `<30` on RSI finds trades made while oversold.
- **Layout:** columns have fixed widths, so the leftover width is one empty strip on the right, which leaves room for more columns later.
- **If Bloomberg is down:** the technicals show "—", and the header says they're unavailable.

These are Bloomberg's own figures (`RSI_14D`, `MOV_AVG_50D`, `MOV_AVG_200D`, `VOLATILITY_30D`), not something the app calculates, so they match the Terminal. I checked both pages in a real browser at your screen width (1900px) with live data. All 118 frontend tests, lint and the type check pass. The tests mock Bloomberg, so they never reach the DeskLink on your machine.

```
import type { ColDef } from 'ag-grid-community'

/**
 * An empty column that takes up the spare width between a grid's own data and the Bloomberg
 * block pinned on the right. It is a real column, so row rules, striping and hover run straight
 * through it and the gap reads as deliberate spacing rather than blank page.
 */
export function spacerColumn<T>(): ColDef<T> {
  return {
    colId: 'spacer',
    headerName: '',
    flex: 1,
    minWidth: 16,
    sortable: false,
    resizable: false,
    suppressMovable: true,
    suppressHeaderMenuButton: true,
    filter: false,
    floatingFilter: false,
    suppressNavigable: true,
    valueGetter: () => null,
    cellClass: 'cell-spacer',
    headerClass: 'cell-spacer',
  }
}

```

</details>

```
export function technicalColumnGroup<T extends TechnicalColumns>(
  headerName: string,
  headerTooltip: string,
): ColGroupDef<T> {
  const column = (
    field: keyof TechnicalColumns,
    header: string,
    width: number,
    tooltip: string,
    extra: Partial<ColDef<T>>,
  ) =>
    ({
      field,
      headerName: header,
      headerTooltip: tooltip,
```

**Claude:**

You're right. I kept patching the symptom instead of fixing the cause, so I'll do it properly this time.

Pinning the Bloomberg columns to the right split the grid into two separate sections. Whenever the main section's columns didn't add up to its width (after a resize, for example), blank space opened up between the two sections and the row lines broke.

The fix:

1. **No pinning.** Every column, Bloomberg included, sits in one continuous section, so each row's border runs edge to edge.
2. **Even widths.** All columns start at the same width, and the grid scales them to fill exactly. A column only gets more if its content needs it: the Name column, the timestamp, or a column's minimum width.
3. **Resizing never leaves a gap.** When you drag a column, it keeps exactly the width you gave it, and the other columns absorb the difference. Resizing the window refits everything. If you widen columns beyond what fits, the grid scrolls sideways rather than leaving blank space.
4. **Bloomberg still reads as separate.** The 50px empty column stays, now with row lines running through it. The Bloomberg columns get accent-coloured headers and a faint tint.

I'll then test real dragging and window resizing in the browser, not just a screenshot.

```
import type {
  ColumnResizedEvent,
  GridApi,
  IColumnLimit,
  SizeColumnsToFitGridStrategy,
} from 'ag-grid-community'

/**
 * Keeps a grid's columns filling its width exactly, so row rules always run edge to edge and no
 * blank band opens up:
 *
 * - On first render, and whenever the grid or its scrollbar changes size, every column is scaled
 *   to fit (AG Grid's continuous fitGridWidth). Columns start from equal widths, so they share the
 *   space evenly unless their minimum (content) needs more.
 * - When the user drags a column, that column keeps exactly the width they gave it and the others
 *   absorb the difference, in proportion. If they cannot (all at their minimum), the grid scrolls
 *   sideways rather than leaving a gap.
 * - `fixedWidths` columns (spacer, expand chevron) never change.
 */
export function fitColumnsToWidth<T>(fixedWidths: Record<string, number>) {
  const fixedLimits: IColumnLimit[] = Object.entries(fixedWidths).map(([key, width]) => ({
    key,
    minWidth: width,
    maxWidth: width,
  }))

  const autoSizeStrategy: SizeColumnsToFitGridStrategy<T> = {
    type: 'fitGridWidth',
    continuous: true,
    columnLimits: Object.entries(fixedWidths).map(([colId, width]) => ({
      colId,
      minWidth: width,
      maxWidth: width,
    })),
  }

  function onColumnResized(event: ColumnResizedEvent<T>) {
    if (!event.finished || event.source !== 'uiColumnResized') return
    const resized = (event.columns ?? []).map((column) => ({
      key: column.getColId(),
      minWidth: column.getActualWidth(),
      maxWidth: column.getActualWidth(),
    }))
    event.api.sizeColumnsToFit({ columnLimits: [...fixedLimits, ...resized] })
  }

  function onGridSizeChanged(event: { api: GridApi<T> }) {
    event.api.sizeColumnsToFit({ columnLimits: fixedLimits })
  }

  return { autoSizeStrategy, onColumnResized, onGridSizeChanged }
}

```

```
import type { Column, ColumnResizedEvent, GridApi, IColumnLimit } from 'ag-grid-community'

/**
 * Keeps a grid's columns filling its width exactly, so row rules always run edge to edge and no
 * blank band opens up beside the last column.
 *
 * - Every column starts from the same width and the grid scales them to fit, so they share the
 *   space evenly unless a column's minimum (its content) needs more.
 * - Columns the user drags keep the width they were given; the remaining columns absorb the
 *   difference in proportion. At least one column is always left free to absorb it (if the user has
 *   sized every column, their oldest choice is released), so a gap can never open. If the free
 *   columns hit their minimums the grid scrolls sideways instead.
 * - The grid refits when it is created, when its rows change (a vertical scrollbar can appear or go
 *   away), when it is resized and after every drag.
 * - `fixedWidths` columns (spacer, expand chevron) never change.
 */
export function fitColumnsToWidth<T>(fixedWidths: Record<string, number>) {
  const fixedIds = new Set(Object.keys(fixedWidths))
  /** Widths the user chose, oldest first. */
  const userWidths = new Map<string, number>()

  const limits = (): IColumnLimit[] =>
    [...Object.entries(fixedWidths), ...userWidths].map(([key, width]) => ({
      key,
      minWidth: width,
      maxWidth: width,
    }))

  function fit(api: GridApi<T>) {
    if (!api.isDestroyed()) api.sizeColumnsToFit({ columnLimits: limits() })
  }

  function onColumnResized(event: ColumnResizedEvent<T>) {
    if (!event.finished || event.source !== 'uiColumnResized') return
    const resized = (event.columns ?? []).map((column: Column) => column.getColId())
    for (const column of event.columns ?? []) {
      userWidths.delete(column.getColId()) // re-insert as the newest choice
      userWidths.set(column.getColId(), column.getActualWidth())
    }
    const free = event.api
      .getAllDisplayedColumns()
      .filter((c) => !fixedIds.has(c.getColId()) && !userWidths.has(c.getColId()))
    if (free.length === 0) {
      const oldest = [...userWidths.keys()].find((id) => !resized.includes(id))
      if (oldest !== undefined) userWidths.delete(oldest)
    }
    fit(event.api)
  }

  const refit = (event: { api: GridApi<T> }) => fit(event.api)

  return {
    onColumnResized,
    onGridReady: refit,
    onFirstDataRendered: refit,
    onRowDataUpdated: refit,
    onGridSizeChanged: refit,
  }
}
```

```
Bloomberg lives on the user's desk, so live prices are fetched **by the browser** from DeskLink's `bdp` route
(`http://localhost:9195/con/bloomberg/bdp`), never through the API. They power two things:

- **The trade ticket:** as a symbol is typed, it waits for a 350 ms pause, then shows the Bloomberg name, last
  price and day change, with **Use** to copy the price into the ticket. A new symbol aborts the lookup in flight,
  so a slow answer for an earlier symbol is never shown.
- **The Positions page** (`/positions`): every open position marked to last price, with market value,
  unrealized and day P&L, and totals (long, short, net and gross exposure). One batched request every 15 seconds.
  Click a row to expand it into a DES-style panel: sector, market cap, P/E, P/B, EV/EBITDA, dividend yield,
  payout and ex-date, 52-week range, beta. It also has a 1Y–5Y daily price chart with the position's average cost
  and its trades (▲ buy, ▼ sell). History is one 5-year `bdh` request per symbol per session.

The blotter and Positions tables are **AG Grid Community** grids with spreadsheet-height rows. Columns sort, resize and
move. Positions rows expand into a full-width panel with the security description (DES-style fields), your trades in
that symbol (each with the position it left) and the price chart. Live-price cells flash when they change.

Both grids end with **Bloomberg technicals**: RSI(14), price against the 50- and 200-day moving averages, and 30-day
volatility. On the blotter they are the figures **on each trade's date** (one `bdh` request for every symbol, once
per session). On Positions they are **current**, compared with the live price, and refreshed every 5 minutes
through DeskLink's 15-minute cache. They filter like any number column: `<30` on RSI finds trades made while
oversold.

Both grids have a **filter row under the column headers**: type in any column, and the columns combine with AND.
Each input takes a small expression language (`app/src/utils/columnFilter.ts`). Hover an input for its syntax, and an
invalid expression turns red and is ignored rather than emptying the table. On the Positions page the summary cards
and totals follow the filters.
```

```
# Trade Blotter

Enter equity trades, watch them appear in a live blotter, and see current positions (net quantity and average cost)
derived from the trade history. Built for the exercise in [docs/trade-blotter-exercise.docx](docs/trade-blotter-exercise.docx).

| Folder | Contents |
| ------ | -------- |
| `api/` | C# / ASP.NET Core Web API on .NET 8: EF Core + SQLite, SignalR, xUnit tests |
| `app/` | Vue 3 (Composition API) + TypeScript + Vite, Pinia, AG Grid Community, Vitest |
| `docs/` | Exercise brief, architecture notes, design decisions |
| `claude/` | How AI (Claude Code) was used, including the session transcript |

## How to run the project locally

Install these once; the run scripts handle everything else (NuGet and npm packages, and the database).

- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 24 LTS (or 22.18+)
```

````
```

or run a script without changing the policy: `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\run_api.ps1`.

### Start the backend and frontend

From the repo root, in two terminals:

```powershell
.\run_api.ps1   # API  -> http://localhost:5035 (Swagger at /swagger), hot reload
.\run_app.ps1   # App  -> http://localhost:5173
```

Open <http://localhost:5173>. In development the blotter starts with a simulated year of 103 trades (see
[Seed data](#seed-data)); book more and open a second browser window to see them arrive live.

| Script | Options |
| ------ | ------- |
| `run_api.ps1` | `-NoWatch` runs without hot reload |
| `run_app.ps1` | `-Install` forces a clean `npm ci` |

- The SQLite database (`api/src/TradeBlotter.Api/trade-blotter.db`) is created and migrated automatically on API
  startup, and seeded if it is empty. Delete the file to start again from the seed.
- `run_app.ps1` installs npm packages on first run and again whenever `package-lock.json` changes.
- Without PowerShell, the equivalent commands are `dotnet watch run --project src/TradeBlotter.Api --launch-profile http`
  from `api/`, and `npm ci && npm run dev` from `app/`.

npm run test:unit -- --run    # Vitest: validation, store, components
npm run type-check            # vue-tsc
npm run lint                  # oxlint + eslint
npm run build                 # type-check + production build
```
````

````bash
""","""## Assumptions and design decisions

More detail in [docs/decisions.md](docs/decisions.md) and [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md).

### Key design choices

- **Typed filters in an AG Grid-style table.** I built the blotter as an AG Grid table, the kind of grid traders
  already work in: dense rows, sortable, resizable and movable columns, and a filter box under every column header.
  The filters are typed expressions rather than dropdowns, so a trader can type `>1000` on Quantity, `ko|pep` on
  Symbol, `2026-09` on Time, or combine conditions with `&`. Columns combine with AND, and an invalid expression is
  flagged and ignored instead of emptying the grid.
- **Every trade field is required.** A trade must have a symbol, a side, a quantity, a price and a timestamp. The
  API rejects a request with any field missing (a `400` naming each one), and the `Trade` domain type cannot be
  created without all five valid values. Quantity is always positive and the side alone gives the direction, so
  "Buy -200" is rejected rather than treated as a short.
- **Desktop data in a remotely hosted app, shown and then set aside.** As a demonstration of bringing data from a
  user's desktop into a web app hosted elsewhere, I added a Positions page and live Bloomberg calls. They are made
  from the browser to DeskLink on the user's own machine, never through the server: live prices and P&L, a DES-style
  security panel, price history charts and Bloomberg technicals. To keep the app on the brief's original focus (trade
  entry, the blotter and positions), these are hidden. The Positions page is not linked from the header (it is
  still reachable at `/positions`), and the technicals columns are hidden in the grids. The trade ticket's live
  price lookup is the one visible piece. On a machine without DeskLink it reports "Live prices unavailable" and
  everything else works normally.
""")
````

**Claude:**

I've added both to the README and committed it (`07cfb75`).

**Quick start**, near the top:
1. Install the .NET 8 SDK and Node.js.
2. Clone the repo and open two terminals.
3. Start the API and the app: `.\run_api.ps1` and `.\run_app.ps1` on Windows, with an equivalent pair of commands for macOS/Linux.
4. Open http://localhost:5173.

It also notes that packages install automatically and the database is created and seeded on first start, so there's nothing else to set up. The fuller run instructions stay below it.

**Key design choices**, at the start of the design section, written as your decisions:
- **Typed filters in an AG Grid-style table:** expressions like `>1000`, `ko|pep` or `2026-09` typed under each column header, rather than dropdowns.
- **Every trade field is required:** the API returns a `400` naming each missing field, and a trade can't be created without all five values. "Buy −200" is rejected rather than treated as a short.
- **Desktop data in a remotely hosted app:** the Positions page and live Bloomberg calls go from the browser to DeskLink on the user's machine, never through the server. They were added as a demonstration, then hidden to keep the app on the brief's focus.

I wrote "Positions page" where you said "trade page", since that's the page we hid. Tell me if you meant something else.

The trade ticket's live Bloomberg price is still visible. It's the one Bloomberg piece left showing, and the README says so. On a machine without DeskLink, which is what a grader will have, it just shows "Live prices unavailable". Do you want that hidden too, so nothing Bloomberg-related shows?

```
#!/usr/bin/env node
// Converts a Claude Code session log (.jsonl) into a readable Markdown transcript.
//
//   node tools/export-transcript.mjs <session.jsonl> <out.md> [title]
//
// Keeps the user's messages, Claude's replies, and every tool call with its result (long
// results shortened). Leaves out content the app injects behind the scenes (<system-reminder>
// blocks, hidden meta messages) and Claude's private reasoning, and redacts email addresses.

import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'

const [, , input, output, title = 'Claude Code session transcript'] = process.argv
if (!input || !output) {
  console.error('usage: node tools/export-transcript.mjs <session.jsonl> <out.md> [title]')
  process.exit(1)
}

const MAX_RESULT = 2500
const MAX_INPUT = 4000

const redact = (text) =>
  text
    .replace(/<system-reminder>[\s\S]*?<\/system-reminder>/g, '')
    .replace(/[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}/g, '[email redacted]')

const clip = (text, max) =>
  text.length > max ? `${text.slice(0, max)}\n… (${text.length - max} more characters)` : text

const fence = (text, lang = '') => {
  const longest = Math.max(2, ...[...text.matchAll(/`+/g)].map((m) => m[0].length))
  const ticks = '`'.repeat(longest + 1)
  return `${ticks}${lang}\n${text}\n${ticks}`
}

const quote = (text) =>
  text
    .trim()
    .split('\n')
    .map((line) => `> ${line}`)
    .join('\n')

function resultText(content) {
  if (typeof content === 'string') return content
  if (!Array.isArray(content)) return ''
  return content
    .map((part) => (part.type === 'text' ? part.text : part.type === 'image' ? '[image]' : ''))
    .join('\n')
}

function describeToolInput(name, input) {
  if (!input || typeof input !== 'object') return ''
  if (name === 'Bash' || name === 'PowerShell') {
    return `${input.description ? `_${input.description}_\n\n` : ''}${fence(clip(input.command ?? '', MAX_INPUT), name === 'Bash' ? 'bash' : 'powershell')}`
  }
  if (name === 'Write') {
    return `\`${input.file_path}\`\n\n${fence(clip(input.content ?? '', MAX_INPUT))}`
  }
  if (name === 'Edit') {
    return `\`${input.file_path}\`\n\n${fence(clip(`- ${input.old_string}\n+ ${input.new_string}`, MAX_INPUT), 'diff')}`
  }
  if (name === 'Read') return `\`${input.file_path}\``
  return fence(clip(JSON.stringify(input, null, 2), MAX_INPUT), 'json')
}

const lines = readFileSync(input, 'utf8').split('\n').filter(Boolean)
const out = [
  `# ${title}`,
  '',
  `Exported from \`${input.split(/[\\/]/).pop()}\` by \`tools/export-transcript.mjs\`.`,
  'Your messages and Claude\'s replies are complete. Tool results longer than ' +
    `${MAX_RESULT} characters are shortened. Content the app injects behind the scenes (system reminders) and ` +
    'Claude\'s private reasoning are left out, and email addresses are redacted.',
  '',
]

let messages = 0
for (const line of lines) {
  let record
  try {
    record = JSON.parse(line)
  } catch {
    continue
  }
  if (record.isMeta || !record.message || (record.type !== 'user' && record.type !== 'assistant')) continue
  const when = record.timestamp ? new Date(record.timestamp).toISOString().replace('T', ' ').slice(0, 19) : ''
  const content = record.message.content
  const parts = typeof content === 'string' ? [{ type: 'text', text: content }] : (content ?? [])

  for (const part of parts) {
    if (part.type === 'text') {
      const text = redact(part.text ?? '').trim()
      if (!text) continue
      if (record.type === 'user') {
        out.push(`---`, '', `### User · ${when}`, '', quote(text), '')
      } else {
        out.push(`**Claude:**`, '', text, '')
      }
      messages++
    } else if (part.type === 'image' && record.type === 'user') {
      out.push('> [image attached]', '')
    } else if (part.type === 'tool_use') {
      out.push(`<details><summary>Tool: <code>${part.name}</code></summary>`, '', redact(describeToolInput(part.name, part.input)), '', '</details>', '')
    } else if (part.type === 't
```
